The active power and reactive power provided by the distributed generation can better balance the load in the system, make the distribution network operate better, and improve the power quality and operation economy of the distribution network.

articleTitle: RESEARCH ON FAULT ANALYSIS TECHNOLOGY FOR PV SYSTEM INTEGRATION WITH DC BOOSTER SYSTEM BASED ON RTDS SIMULATOR
abstract: This paper mainly studies the photovoltaic modules after the DC-DC booster through four collection branches, into the ±30kV collection bus, and then through the DC output line access to MMC grid converter, after inverter into 35kV AC system. Based on RTDS(Real Time Digital Simulator) Platform real-time simulation platform, the dynamic operation characteristics and fault response characteristics of photovoltaic DC collection system are deeply studied in this paper. The simulation results show that the proposed control strategy can meet the requirements of the photovoltaic array working at the maximum power point and ensure the stability of DC voltage and power balance of the system. The faults such as single-phase grounding of AC line, single-pole grounding of DC collecting branch and bipolar short circuit of DC collecting branch in photovoltaic DC boosting collecting access system are analyzed, which provide the basis for parameter setting and protection value setting of control and protection device.

articleTitle: Wind Turbine Generator Bearing Early Fault Warning Based on Feature Fusion and XGBoost
abstract: Aiming to realize the fault diagnosis of bearing in wind turbine generators, through the Condition Monitoring System (CMS) vibration data. A algorithm based on feature fusion and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) is designed. The algorithm consists of two parts. The first part is the feature fusion algorithm, which extracts time domain characteristics, frequency domain characteristics, trend characteristics, envelope characteristics from vibration data and combines these characteristics into a feature vector as the input of the fault identification algorithm. The second part is the XGBoost fault identification algorithm. A generator bearing fault identification model based on XGBoost is established to identify two fault types of generator bearing, which are wear failure and loose failure.The results of the example show that the feature fusion algorithm can capture the early abnormal features of the generator bearing, and XGBoost can identify different fault types more accurately than other algorithms.

articleTitle: Efficient hole-transport layer free perovskite solar cell with perovskite homojunction
abstract: Hole-transport layer free perovskite solar cells (HTL-free PSCs) have attracted much attention due to low production cost and high device stability. However, the efficiency of such devices cannot compete with devices with HTL. Here, we propose the HTL-free PSCs device structure with perovskite homojunction. wxAMPS software is used to optimize some parameters that affect the performance of the device, such as the thickness of perovskite absorption layer, the proportion of n-type and p-type layers and doping concentration, and an efficiency of more than 19% is obtained. It is found that in order to obtain a high-efficiency HTL-free device, the ratio of p-type perovskite layer to total absorber layer should be 0.2 and heavily doped, while the doping concentration of n-type layer should be reduced. This work has laid a theoretical foundation for the preparation of efficient HTL-free PSCs.

articleTitle: ADAPTIVE EVENT-TRIGGERED LOAD FREQUENCY CONTROL FOR MULTI-AREA POWER SYSTEMS UNDER DECEPTION ATTACKS
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the load frequency control (LFC) for multi-area power systems based on the sampleddata-based event-triggered communication. The controller is presented for guaranteeing the stabilization of the considered LFC model under the proposed event-triggered mechanism, which notably reduce the cost of control and communication. Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional method are employed to achieve the aforementioned control goal. Finally, a three-area networked power system is used to show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: HYBRID AVERAGE-VALUE MODELLING OF DFIG-BASED WIND ENERGY CONVERSION SYSTEMS
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid average-value model (AVM) of doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG)-based wind energy conversion systems (WECSs). As an efficient and accurate electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation model, the hybrid AVM is able to address the full operating conditions of DFIG-WECSs, including normal conditions and grid fault conditions. Noticeably, the hybrid AVM can effectively deal with the switching transients of power electronic devices and the switching of the system structure, such as the crowbar protective switching under the grid fault conditions. By comparing the simulation results with the detailed EMT model, the accuracy of the hybrid AVM is demonstrated, while the simulation efficiency is drastically improved. Therefore, the hybrid AVM is promising in EMT-type dynamic simulations of power systems containing a large number of DFIG-WECSs.

articleTitle: Multi-PV Interfaced Distribution Network fault analysis method considering LVRT control strategy
abstract: With the increasing penetration of photovoltaic power stations (PV) in the distribution network, and the ability of low voltage ride through (LVRT) for PV, which is under PQ control, has become the latest grid-connection regulation. The existing fault analysis methods have some deficiencies. This paper first analyses the output current characteristics of PV fault under PQ control strategy. The influence of PV distribution on the electrical parameters is demonstrated. Combing with the characteristics of PQ control strategy, the effect of fault types on the fault characteristics analysis of distribution network with multiple PV access is analyzed. On this basis, a fault analysis method for multi-PV interfaced distribution network considering fault types and PV distribution is proposed. Finally, the accuracy of the proposed method is verified by comparing the simulation results with the existing methods.

articleTitle: Modeling Method of OPLC Thermal Circuit Model based on Superposition Principle
abstract: Optical fiber composite low-voltage cable which combines optical fiber and power cable organically plays an important role in the construction of smart grid and the development of energy internet. The change of temperature impacts the working state of the OPLC and the precision of parameter measurement. Thus, the establishment of the OPLC thermal circuit model has important practical significance. Focusing on the attributes of different kinds and various constructions of the OPLC, this paper proposes an OPLC modeling method based on the superposition principle. Firstly, the asymmetric OPLC is equivalent to several symmetric sub-models, and then each model is superimposed by superposition principle. Secondly, the particle swarm algorithm is utilized to realize the model boundary distinguishing identification, improve the accuracy of the parameters, acquire a precise thermal circuit model, and then realize the accurate calculation of temperature at different positions of OPLC. This paper establishes an OPLC thermal circuit model based on the four-cable core OPLC and proves the effectiveness of the method through simulation analysis and experimental verification.

articleTitle: FUNCTIONAL COMPOSITED MMC SUB MODULES TOPOLOGY DESIGN AND CONTROL
abstract: Modular multilevel converters have become one of the most technologically advantageous converter topologies in the field of high voltage direct current and power conversion. As its basic structural unit, although the half-bridge sub module topology has the advantages of simple structure, low cost and low power losses, it lacks the capability of DC fault current limitation, which restricts its application of low-cost overhead lines in high voltage transmission. At the same time, the cascade of large quantum sub modules will also have capacitor voltage equalization problem. In this paper, a functional complex sub module (FCSM) topology with DC fault suppression ability is proposed based on the idea of blocking suppression and clamping circuit to solve the above problems. Compared with the traditional HBSM topology, the proposed FCSM can realize the self-equalizing of the internal capacitor voltage of the sub-module without additional hardware cost. According to the negative level output characteristics of the topology, the non-latching DC fault suppression strategy is also studied. Finally, simulation results are carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed topology.

articleTitle: BILATERAL INERTIA AND DAMPING EMULATION CONTROL SCHEME OF VSC-HVDC TRANSMISSION SYSTEMS FOR ASYNCHRONOUS GRID INTERCONNECTIONS
abstract: This paper proposes a novel control scheme which realizes the bilateral inertia and damping emulation (BIDE) control scheme of the voltage source converter based high voltage DC (VSC-HVDC) transmission systems for asynchronous grid interconnections. Under the proposed BIDE scheme, the VSC-HVDC systems can autonomously and simultaneously provide the emulated inertial and damping responses to the two interconnected asynchronous AC systems in a similar fashion of synchronous generators, which can effectively enhance the stability and damp the frequency oscillations for both of the AC systems. The energy for providing the inertial effect comes from the augmented DC capacitance installed on the DC link and the energy for providing the damping effect comes from the AC systems connected on the both sides. The effectiveness of the proposed BIDE scheme is demonstrated in a point-to-point VSC-HVDC system model simulated in MATLAB/Simulink environment in the presence of load changes on each side respectively.

articleTitle: STOCHASTIC UNIT COMMITMENT INCORPORATIING WIND POWER USING IMPROVED GENETIC ALGORITHM
abstract: With the increasing penetration level of wind power integration, its uncertainty has brought a series of challenges to the optimal operation of modern power grids. Based on the interval forecast method, this paper establishes a unit commitment model incorporating wind farms. Regarding the highly discrete and nonlinear characteristics of the established optimization model, an enhanced genetic algorithm based on the unified encoding technique of real and binary numbers is proposed to solve the problem. Among them, a two-dimensional real matrix is used to describe the generation schedule directly, which greatly reduces the storage space and calculation time, and at the same time, the binary matrix that transformed from the real matrix is combined to simulate the up/down state of the units. In addition, a heuristic constraints processing method is adopted to dynamically modify the real matrix and binary matrix, and thus ensures that the minimum up/down time constraints and spinning reserve constraints can be satisfied fully. Moreover, a dynamic priority list method based on the slight increase rate of coal consumption curve is proposed to handle the economic dispatch. Finally, the 10-unit and 20-unit test systems are taken to verify the validity of the proposed model and algorithm.

articleTitle: Planning Method of Power Grid with High Penetration of Renewable Energy Considering the Correlation between Wind Power and Photovoltaic
abstract: Current situation of energy shortage and environmental pollution have been alleviated with the rapid development of new energy sources represented by wind power and photovoltai c. Simultaneously, the intermittency, volatility and correlation of new energy sources induce new challenges to power system planning. Output of wind farms and photovoltaic stations mainly presents complementarities, only in a few time periods showing weak correlation, which means that probabilities to get the maximum output of both at the same time are very small. The current transmission network planning mostly adopts the installed capacities of wind farms and photovoltaic power stations. Although the sec urity is satisfied, it may result in overinvestment, waste of resources and sacrifice of economy. In this paper, firstly based on the direct current power flow algorithm, the transmission network planning model considering the correlations of the output be tween wind farms and photovoltaic stations is established. Then, according to the characteristics of the planning model, an improved particle swarm optimization algorithm is proposed. Finally, the proposed planning model and optimization algorithm are util ized in the extended IEEE system with 24 nodes to obtain the optimal cost planning scheme, which can satisfy all typical scenarios and extreme scenarios. Compared with the scenario planning scheme when the correlation is not considered, which means that ma ximum capacities of wind farms and photovoltaic stations are taken at the same time, the necessity of considering the correlations of output from wind farms and photovoltaic stations in the transmission network planning is discussed.

articleTitle: A PATTERN RECOGNITION METHOD TO IDENTIFY THE ROOT FAULTS DURING ALARM FLOODS
abstract: Alarm systems can provide comprehensive monitoring of wind turbines and give useful information to remote technicians. However, most of the current alarm systems are suffering from the alarm flood, which means tens or hundreds of alarms appear in a short period of time. This alarm flood overwhelms the operator and requires extensive domain knowledge to interpret. This paper proposes a pattern recognition method using the alarm floods generated during a fault. The aim is to identify the root faults of alarm floods and assist the operator in decision making. Initially, the FP-growth algorithm is applied to extract the related alarms. The related alarms are expressed as the alarm vectors based on the defined rules in this paper. Subsequently, the key alarm vectors of faults are generated based on the maintenance record. Ultimately, the Hamming distance and the Jaccard distance are used to compare the unknown alarm vectors to the key alarm vectors. The performance of the distances is assessed using three defined indicators. The proposed method is verified using actual data from two wind turbines. The results show that the proposed method can identify the root faults of alarm floods effectively.

articleTitle: SEQUENCE IMPEDANCE MODELING AND ANALYSIS OF PMSG WIND TURBINES CONSIDERING THE ELECTROMECHANICAL COUPLING
abstract: With the continuous increasing installing proportion of the permanent magnet synchronous generators wind turbines (PMSG-WTs), oscillation issues in grid-connecting PMSG wind farms are observed frequently. Sequence impedance model has gradually become a widely used method to analyze grid-connecting wind power oscillation issues. The sequence impedance model of PMSG-WTs built before usually ignores the torsional interaction between the shaft mechanical subsystem and the electrical subsystem, as called electromechanical coupling effect. This paper investigates the impact of the shaft mechanical model on the output electrical impedance characteristic of the PMSG-WTs. The dynamic behavior of the shaft subsystem is modeled through two-mass-spring mechanical model. Then the output sequence impedance model of PMSG-WT considering the electromechanical coupling effect is obtained, reflecting the transfer relationship of the small-signal perturbation between the shaft mechanical subsystem and the electrical subsystem.

articleTitle: Short Circuit Fault Analysis of DC Grid Based on Electric Quantity
abstract: In DC grid, the transient stability of DC voltage and fault crossing ability count for much. In this paper,the dynamic model of a flexible DC power grid was initially established. Then, combined with the fault process and related characteristics of bipolar short circuit ,the principle of equal electrical quantity which should be followed in the transient recovery of multi terminal DC grid is proposed, and the limit fault clearing time is deduced based on this principle. Finally, a simulation model of the multi terminal DC power network is built, and the results of a numerical example verify the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed theory.

articleTitle: Research on Wake Characteristics of NREL 5MW Wind Turbine with LBM-LES Method
abstract: Wake is the main reason for the loss of power generation in wind farms. Exploring the characteristics of wind turbine wake is of great significance to the development of wind power. This paper applied the LBM-LES method to numerically simulate the New MEXICO wind turbine and compared them with the experimental values to verify the reliability of the model. The results show that the LBM-LES method captures the details and characteristics of the complex unsteady flow field of the wind turbine. The NREL 5MW offshore wind turbine was used to study the constant wake characteristics of wind turbines under non-turbulent and turbulent inflow conditions. Under turbulent inflow conditions, the wake field presents obvious turbulence characteristics, the tip vortex, and root vortex are destroyed earlier and dissipated into small-scale vortices. The vortex structures of various scales induce and interact with each other, and the turbulence intensity of the incoming flow is conducive to the recovery of wake velocity, and in the near wake region, the distribution of the tip vortex is similar to non-turbulent condition.

articleTitle: HIGH-PRECISION AND SYNCHRONIZED WIDEBAND MEASUREMENT TECHNOLOGY AND ITS APPLICATIONS
abstract: To enhance the monitoring capability of the operation situation in wide frequency band of power systems integrated with large-scale power electronic devices, the wideband synchronized measurement unit (WMU) has been developed using the embedded DSP-FPGA computing module based on fast noise filter and fast tuning TFT wideband measurement algorithm. The WMU has been integrated with 5G communication technology, which can meet the communication needs of multi scenarios. The high-speed transmission of wideband measurement data is realized using the optical fiber communication and 5G/4G wireless communication. The potential applications of WMU mainly include the wideband oscillation monitoring, the wideband parameter identification, the wideband disturbance localization, the high-precision power quality assessment, the wideband feature driven fault identification, the post-mortem wideband disturbance analysis, and the wideband transfer characteristics testing of electrical devices.

articleTitle: ANALYSIS OF THE AMPLITUDE AND FREQUENCY CHARACTERISTIC OF STEAM TURBINE GENERATOR'S INTERNAL VOLTAGE UNDER ASYMMETRIC FAULT IN SERIES COMPENSATION SYSTEM
abstract: A thermal power transmission system via series capacitor compensation is a common transmission method in the power system. The series capacitor compensation is utilized to improve the transmission capacity of the transmission line. However, it may cause rotor shaft torque amplification of the steam turbine generator during the transient process, and especially have a non-negligible impact on internal voltage amplitude and frequency characteristics of the generator under the system asymmetric fault. Based on the rotor shaft model of the steam turbine generator in the IEEE sub-synchronous oscillation first benchmark model, the no-load internal voltage expression of the steam turbine generator considering the shaft oscillation is calculated in this paper firstly. Furthermore, the influence of the rotor mode on the generator's internal voltage under the series compensation system asymmetric fault is obtained by analytical calculation, and the amplitude and frequency timevarying characteristics are summarized. Finally, the corresponding system model is built in PSCAD/EMTDC to verify the correctness of the analytical expression and time-varying characteristic of the internal voltage.

articleTitle: Research on MMC control strategy based on offshore wind farm
abstract: For large-scale and long-distance deep-sea wind farms, traditional HVDC is no longer applicable. MMC-HVDC, as a new HVDC grid-connected technology, can meet the requirements of high-power long-distance transmission. Aiming at the phenomenon of capacitor voltage imbalance during MMC normal operation, a voltage balance scheme with gating signal rotation is proposed based on the carrier in-phase cascade modulation strategy. To verify the effectiveness of the scheme, a set of simulation model is built based on MATLAB / Simulink simulation platform, and the simulation test is carried out. The results show that the control scheme can effectively balance MMC capacitor voltage.

articleTitle: RESEARCH ON A CROSSING BIPOLAR THREE LEVEL SUB MODULE TOPOLOGY AND ITS CONTROL STRATEGIES
abstract: When the modular multilevel converter based on the half bridge sub module topology is applied to high voltage dc transmission, it does not have the ability to block dc short circuit fault current, which affects the application of low-cost overhead lines. In order to achieve dc fault suppression, a new crossing single pole three level sub module topology is studied to solve the problem of unbalanced charging of hybrid topology capacitors. At the same time, in order to cope with the possible adverse effects of blocking suppression on the converter and the power grid, a positive and negative bipolar level output sub module topology is designed, the number of power devices is further reduced and their control strategies are studied. Finally, the simulation model is built in PSCAD/EMTDC, and the dc fault suppression characteristics of the crossing bipolar three level sub module topology are simulated and verified.

articleTitle: Predictive Current Control Strategy of Three-phase PWM Rectifier under Power Network Unbalance
abstract: The traditional three-phase PWM rectifier predictive control will cause the grid-connected current distortion, the increase of harmonics and the decrease of system reliability when the grid is unbalanced. In this paper, a predictive current control method based on virtual flux is proposed. In order to improve the accuracy of observation, a flux observer with an in-band compensation link was established in the system. Because there is a certain error in the network voltage estimated by this method, the control system is constructed by using the backward prediction two-step current control strategy and combining with the new power theory, which can solve the problems such as the lag and error in the signal acquisition of the system and the great power fluctuation caused by the power grid fault. The simulation results show that the flux tracking network voltage is accurate, the current distortion and power ripple are suppressed, and the system has good performance.

articleTitle: LSTM load forecasting algorithm based on time-sharing somatosensory
abstract: With economic development, people's living standards have gradually improved, and the use of air conditioners and other electrical equipment has increased year by year, which directly leads to the increasing impact of meteorological factors on power load. The temperature adjustment load caused by the extensive use of air conditioners in summer has proved to be closely related to meteorological factors such as temperature, humidity, and wind speed. As a basic model, LSTM can maximize the time-series and non-linear relationship between data when predicting power load data. However, this network tends to ignore the influencing factors that lead to sudden changes in load data. This paper conducts comprehensive modeling analysis based on minute-level meteorological factors, obtains the change value of load through the change of body temperature, and obtains the time series forecast value of load through LSTM, and then obtains the final forecast value. The forecast results show that this method can effectively improve the accuracy of short-term load forecasting and is an effective load forecasting method.

articleTitle: RESEARCH ON OVER VOLTAGE RIDE THROUGH ADAPTABILITY AND CONTROL OPTIMIZATION OF WIND FARM
abstract: According to the standard, the over voltage ride through assessment point of wind farm is the over voltage side bus of main transformer, and the over voltage ride through test point of wind turbine is the 35kV side of the box transformer. Affected by the impedance of the collection system in the wind farm, the over voltage ride through response of the wind farm and the wind turbine may not be consistent. In this paper, the adaptability of wind farm over voltage ride through is analyzed. Establish equivalent circuit model of wind farm, and analyze voltage distribution in the wind farm when the voltage of the point of connection rises. The main factors affecting the difference between wind turbine and wind farm are extracted. Considering the constraints of wind farm and wind turbine voltage operation, the measures to optimize the operation parameters of the wind farm electrical equipment is proposed, in order to improve the over voltage ride through capacity of the wind farm. Taking an actual wind farm as an example, the simulation results show that the theoretical analysis is correct, and the effectiveness of the proposed measures is verified.

articleTitle: Frequency-Domain Identification Method for Controller Parameters of PMSG-Based Wind Power Conversion System Based on Vector Fitting
abstract: Permanent-magnetic synchronous generator (PMSG) based wind power conversion system (WPCS) usually contains multi-band control links for both machine-side converter (MSC) and grid-side converter (GSC), including inner and outer loops as well as phase-locked loop (PLL), and the controller parameters are often unknowable, that is, there is a “grey box” problem. In order to accurately identify the control parameters of various control links with different bandwidths, a frequency-domain identification method based on port admittance characteristics is proposed. The identification method separately identifies the control parameters of MSC and GSC. First, the dc-port admittance model of MSC and the ac-port dq admittance model of GSC are established to get the theoretical admittance standard formula. Second, the Vector Fitting (VF) algorithm is performed on the measured admittance data to obtain the fitted admittance standard formula. Finally, the controller parameters can be identified by applying the least square principle to minimize the sum of squares of the difference between the coefficients of the corresponding terms in the theoretical admittance standard formula and the fitted admittance standard formula. A case study shows that the proposed method is able to accurately identify all controller parameters with different bandwidths.

articleTitle: Research on Control Strategy of Energy Storage Participating in Primary Frequency Regulation of Power Grid
abstract: The output of new energy generation has volatility and uncertainty, and does not have the inertial response characteristics of traditional power sources. Large scale connection will aggravate the pressure of power grid frequency regulation, and the rapid response characteristics of energy storage battery make it have significant advantages in participating in power grid frequency regulation. In this paper, a droop control strategy based on droop control for primary frequency regulation of power grid is proposed. The strategy takes into account the state of charge (SOC) of energy storage battery through real-time acquisition of grid frequency, and reasonably controls the charge and discharge of energy storage battery according to different frequency intervals, so as to respond to the frequency change of power grid quickly and play a role in supporting the frequency recovery of the system. Finally, the effectiveness of the control strategy is verified by the actual case simulation.

articleTitle: Study on the Selection of Transient Characteristic Frequency Band of Power Network Low Frequency Oscillating Disturbance Source Line
abstract: In order to effectively utilize the fault information contained in the line transient characteristic frequency band and accurately select the line transient characteristic frequency band, so that the transient component of the frequency in the frequency band can effectively reflect the location of the low frequency oscillation disturbance source of the power grid, an algorithm for selecting the line transient characteristics of the low frequency oscillation disturbance source of the power grid is proposed. The frequency characteristics of line boundary are analyzed and the frequency band limit constraints of line transient characteristics are obtained. The beginning and end of the low frequency oscillation disturbance source line are regarded as ports. The equivalent impedance of the line is obtained by two-port network equation, and the transient characteristics are analyzed. On this basis, the phase of frequency component and frequency component of current in different lines is extracted by matrix beam method, sorted in ascending order, and the phase of different frequency component is compared. The frequency corresponding to the 90 degree phase angle will be taken as the frequency band limit to complete the selection of the transient characteristic frequency band of the power network low frequency oscillation disturbance source line.

articleTitle: Self-damping fault ride-through control of DFIG for weak grid
abstract: Under the condition that large-scale renewable energy is connected to the weak grid, the operation control between the renewable energy power generation and power grid will be coupled and affected by the dynamic characteristics of the grid-connected point voltage. When a grid fault occurs or the fault is restored, the impedance of the access system changes further, and the traditional fault ride-through (FRT) control strategy of wind turbine is facing adaptability problems under weak grid conditions. For the FRT problem of large-scale renewable energy access to a weak grid, the transient stability of large-scale renewable energy integration into weak grid is studied, and further a self-damping FRT control of DFIG is proposed. Finally, the influence of short circuit fault to the stability of large-scale DFIG based wind turbines integration weak grid are analysed with the simulation results, where the different FRT control strategies are adopted.

articleTitle: Co-Optimal Placement of PMUs and Associated Edge Access Networks in Wide-Area Measurement System Considering Cyber Contingencies
abstract: Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs) based on modern Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs) have been extensively installed to monitor power systems' dynamic processes. Conventional Optimal PMU Placement (OPP) studies mainly focus on measurement observability but neglect the communication failures when cyber contingencies occur. Meanwhile, it is unwise to blindly deploy more PMUs to improve measurement redundancy against cyber contingencies, which could not strengthen the system's resilience but increase the expenditure of associated edge access communication infrastructures. This paper extends the conventional OPP to a Co-Optimal Placement of PMUs and their associated Edge Access Networks (COPPEAN), considering the power systems' full observability and enough resilience against cyber contingencies. A model with minimum total investment as the optimization objective is introduced to solve where the PMUs are installed, where the edge access devices are deployed, and how to construct communication paths between them. Furthermore, the key constraints are proposed by simultaneously considering the observability of both measurement and communication levels. In order to improve the efficiency, the COPPEAN with nonlinear constraints is transformed into the Integer Linear Programming (ILP) framework. Different-scale IEEE standard test systems are employed to verify the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Condition Monitoring Strategy for Modular Multilevel Converters with Improved Accuracy
abstract: The reliability is one issue of great importance for the modular multilevel converters (MMCs). The capacitor is one of the weakest components in the MMC. To estimate the health status of capacitors, condition monitoring (CM) is considered as an effective method and has been widely applied in many MMC applications. This paper proposed a capacitor condition monitoring method for the MMC with improved accuracy, which considers the effect of the capacitor voltage measurement unit. The proposed method employs the dc voltage shift control (DVSC) to ensures the low capacitance estimation error. Finally, the simulation and experimental verifications are conducted to confirm the effectiveness of the proposed monitoring method.

articleTitle: DIAGNOSIS OF BLADE ICING CONDITION OF WIND TURBINES BASED ON RANDOM FOREST
abstract: The icing of wind turbine blades will reduce the reliability of wind turbines, the safety of equipment and personnel, and the stability of power systems, thus the diagnosis of wind turbine blade icing condition is significant. In this paper, the supervisory control and data acquisition system (SCADA) data are used to build the icing diagnostic model based on random forest (RF). First, divide the SCADA data into icing data, non-icing data, and invalid data according to the labels for the data-icing and non-icing; then, use the down-sampling technology to extract a new sample set to avoid unbalanced distribution of sample; finally, the new sample set is applied to RF and compare with other machine learning algorithms such as support vector machine (SVM) and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). The results show that the diagnosis model based on the RF classifier has higher accuracy and precision, and it is more suitable for the practical application of icing diagnosis.

articleTitle: ONLINE FAULT LOCATION FOR UNDERSEA OBSERVATION NETWORKS BASED ON ACTIVE HARMONIC INJECTION
abstract: In the undersea observation networks, most of the fault location methods require to cut off the power supply or to isolate the fault. To avoid power failure, this paper proposes a new fault location method for undersea observation networks based on active harmonic injection. The voltage of Branch Unit (BU) as well as spur cable currents are obtained from the measurements at the junction boxes. When the submarine cable is damaged and a ground short-circuit fault occurs, the shore station outputs periodic harmonic voltage, of which the magnitude on each node differs from fault location. By constructing the nodal harmonic admittance matrix of the main grid, the resistance from the fault to the nearest node is calculated thus obtaining the fault distance. The fault location can be quickly located as soon as the fault occurs, and the fault location is performed without disconnecting the power supply of the shore station, thus online fault location is realized. PSCAD simulation proves that the proposed method is accurate in positioning for multi types of faults in the undersea observation networks power system.

articleTitle: Multi objective operation optimization of multi energy coupling integrated energy system
abstract: The integrated energy system can realize the comprehensive utilization of multiple energy sources, reduce resource waste, increase energy utilization efficiency, and reduce operating costs, thereby building an energy-saving, environmentally-friendly and efficient energy system, but the existing models still need to be improved. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-energy complementary integrated energy system model and analyses a calculation example. This article first established the operation model of the integrated energy system, and carried out simulation calculations based on the four seasons in a certain area of northern China. Second, explored the influence of different waste heat distribution ratios on the operation of the integrated energy system. Third, the weight analysis method is used to make a multi-objective plan for the comprehensive energy system in terms of economy, environmental protection and conservation. The results show that the integrated energy system constructed in this paper can operate effectively and has practical significance. Compared with the distribution system, the cost is greatly reduced. Generally speaking, the model has played an important supporting role in the construction and optimized operation of the actual integrated energy system.

articleTitle: FEASIBILITY ANALYSIS OF USING SOLAR ENERGY FOR COMPRESSOR NAMPAK GLASS INDUSTRY
abstract: Glass making is one of the most energy intensive industries in some countries such as Belgium, China, France, Germany and South Africa. Most of the energy is consumed in the furnace for melting the raw materials. The furnace uses both natural gas and electricity to melt the power demand. The second biggest consumer of electrical energy is the compressor. The compressor system provides both low pressure (LP) and high pressure (HP) air to the furnace and the glass making machines. By using solar energy to power the compressor system, the energy demand from the municipal grid can be greatly reduced. This paper presents the feasibility of supplying Nampak Glass's compressor system with a photovoltaic (PV) system. By comparing the cost of running the compressor system using solar and running the system using municipal energy, a decision will be made on which is the best form of energy to use. This paper aims at finding ways of reducing the energy drawn from the grid in favour of a clean and renewable energy source.

articleTitle: UNTRANSPOSED TRANSMISSION LINE PARAMETER ESTIMATION WITH FULLY DISTRIBUTED PARAMETER MODEL USING SYNCHRONIZED/UNSYNCHRONIZED MEASUREMENTS
abstract: Accurate transmission line parameter estimation is essential for best performances of many applications in practical power systems. This paper proposes a parameter estimation method for untransposed transmission lines in phasor domain using synchronized or unsynchronized phasor voltage and current measurements at dual terminals of the line. The line is represented with fully distributed parameter model in phasor domain, with full consideration of line asymmetry of untransposed lines. The line model includes not only unknown transmission line parameters, but also synchronization angle between the measurements at both terminals of the line, to ensure that the algorithm could work even with unsynchronized measurements. Afterwards, the line parameters as well as the synchronization angle are obtained by solving the line model using state estimation. Numerical experiments in PSCAD/EMTDC verify the estimation accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: WIND SPEED PROBABILISTIC FORECASTING BASED ON THE CORRELATION BETWEEN WIND PATTERNS AND PREDICTION ERRORS
abstract: Although the current use of probabilistic prediction in power system is limited, some researches on wind power probabilistic forecast have appeared to promote the adoption of probabilistic forecasts. There are some problems, such as the width of prediction interval (PI) remains unchanged regardless of the fluctuation of wind speed. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel probabilistic forecast method based on the correlation between wind process fluctuation patterns and prediction errors, using a regularized extreme learning machine (RELM) approach. It is observed that the point prediction error corresponding to the large fluctuation wind process is usually larger than that of the gentle wind process. By clustering the wind processes into four categories to identify different fluctuation degrees, PIs are established for different categories respectively, and a probabilistic forecast result that the width of PIs changes with the fluctuation of wind speed curves is obtained. Through the comparison of the prediction interval width under the same confidence level, it is concluded that the model based on wind pattern recognition can improve the prediction reliability on the premise of ensuring the sharpness of the prediction results.

articleTitle: FEASIBILITY STUDIES ON BLACK START CAPABILITY OF DISTRIBUTED ENERGY RESOURCES
abstract: Power systems are experiencing massive changes in their generation patterns with increasing penetration of decentralised renewable generation and decommissioning of thermal plants. Such changes in generation patterns will bring significant challenges to the black start arrangement. Conventional black start process relies on large thermal plants connected at the transmission level to energise the system using a “top-down” approach. This may no longer be adequate or applicable in future networks due to the closure of most thermal plants. This paper will investigate the feasibility of using Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) to provide a “bottom-up” black start approach. Compared with the conventional approach, using DERs for black start has potential advantages of reduced restoration time and more flexible recovery procedure. In this paper, a comprehensive review of the existing black start studies utilising DERs will be provided. Additionally, several case studies using a distribution network model containing multiple resources such as wind, micro-hydro generator, and energy storage will be presented to demonstrate the feasibility of providing black start capability by DERs. Furthermore, the associated technical issues that need to be considered to enable such a black start approach will also be discussed, along with feasible solutions and suggestions for further investigation.

articleTitle: PRESCRIBED-TIME DISTRIBUTED SECONDARY FREQUENCY CONTROL OF MICROGRIDS WITH TIME DELAYS
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the prescribed-time distributed secondary frequency control problem of the microgrid with time-varying heterogeneous time delays. Namely, the controlled output states of all distributed generations (DGs) can be regulated to its corresponding target values at arbitrary prescribed time instants. Two novel prescribedtime control algorithms are presented for guaranteeing the synchronization of frequency restoration among DGs, meanwhile achieving the optimal active power sharing. With the proposed control algorithms, the negative effect of time delays can be fully compensated by compensation terms, and the actual convergence time is equal to the prescribed time without time delay. The Lyapunov stability theory is employed to obtain the sufficient criteria on the control parameters for the above control objective. Finally, simulation results are provided for demonstrating the effectiveness of the presented control algorithms.

articleTitle: DISTANCE PROTECTION ON MMC-HVDC TRANSMISSION LINES WITH SINGLE-ENDED MEASUREMENTS
abstract: MMC-HVDC grid is a promising way to incorporate a large number of renewable generations. Protection of transmission lines is essential to guarantee the safe operation of the grid during line faults. However, the protection of MMC-HVDC lines requires very high operational speed (typically within 3ms), without losing dependability and security of the protection. This paper proposes a novel distance protection for MMC-HVDC transmission lines. The method only utilizes single-ended measurements, and no communication channels between line terminals are required. First, the model of the transmission line with fault is derived, with the line resistance and inductance “seen” by the relay as the unknown variables. Afterwards, the state estimation procedure is applied to accurately estimate the resistance/inductance. Finally, the trip signal and the faulted pole are determined by comparing the calculated resistance/inductance with the relay characteristics. Numerical experiments in PSCAD/EMTDC show that the proposed method can dependably operate during internal faults within 3ms after the occurrence of the fault, and securely ignore external faults. The calculation burden of the algorithm is small to enable real-time operation of the proposed distance protection method.

articleTitle: Large-disturbance Stability Boundary and Instability Pattern of Grid-connected VSC
abstract: The transient behaviors of power electronic devices are quite different from synchronous generators (SGs), which greatly changes the characteristics of large-disturbance stability of the system. This paper focuses on the stability boundary and the instability patterns of a voltage source converter (VSC) connected to infinity bus (IB). A reduced-order large-signal nonlinear model of the system is first built. The stable equilibrium point (SEP) and the unstable equilibrium point (UEP) are calculated, and the projection of the stability boundary on a sectional plane in the state space through the SEP and the UEP is analyzed. Different from the stability boundary of traditional power system with SGs, the stability boundary of VSC-IB system consists not only stable manifolds of type 1 UEP, but also unstable limit cycle. Correspondingly, the instability patterns include monotonic instability and oscillatory instability.

articleTitle: Fault diagnosis of wind turbine planetary gearbox under variable operating conditions
abstract: Fault diagnosis of planetary gearbox is crucial to reduce unexpected downtime and economic loss of wind turbines (WTs). However, fluctuating operating conditions cause variations in monitored features, which makes the identification of faults a difficult task. Moreover, the massive data from recent condition monitoring systems increases the difficulty of this research. And the traditional machine learning methods heavily depend on well-selected features. In this paper, a fault diagnosis method is proposed based on auto encoder (AE), which is a purely unsupervised feature learning model. Firstly, the massive vibration signals under variable operating conditions are divided into several data segments. Then, the common time-domain features are extracted from these data segments. After that, K-fold cross validation method is used to determine the appropriate number of hidden layer unites of AE network, and the AE model is constructed. Finally, the features are fed into the AE model for fault pattern classification. The performance of the proposed method is cross-verified by the vibration signals from wind turbine driven test rig. The results with multisensors data is compared with single sensor data in this paper. Though comparing with other methods, the superiority of the proposed method is verified.

articleTitle: State Averaging Model based on Dynamic Processes Analysis of Marine Pulsed Load System
abstract: In the modern marine integrated power system (IPS), DC/DC converter is wildly used to improve its carrying capacity of pulsed loads. However, because of the different switching periods between pulsed load and DC/DC converter, the Pulsed Power System (PPS), composed of the DC/DC converter and pulsed loads, has characteristics of complex switching dynamic processes, which makes the traditional state-space averaging PPS model with converter switching period as the averaging operator cannot reflect the dynamic characteristics of PPS. For this reason, this paper analyses the dynamic process of PPS in different combinations of switch states by considering the different switching frequency characteristics of PPS converter and pulse load, proposes a calculation method for the converter total on-off time in dynamic process by taking the pulsed load period instead of traditional converter switch period as averaging operator, and then a presents millisecond-time-scale-based state space averaging model (MTS-SSAM). Finally, the ship integrated power system with PPS is established in Matlab/Simulink, and the simulation results show that the proposed model is effective for analysing the dynamic characteristics of PPS.

articleTitle: STUDY ON THE FUNCTION AND QUANTITATIVE EVALUATION INDEX OF PUMPED-STORAGE POWER STATION SUPPORTING POWER SYSTEM OPERATION
abstract: The new power system with new energy as the main body puts forward further requirements for the functional positioning of pumped-storage power stations. The current functional evaluation of pumped-storage power station is mainly focused on qualitative evaluation. Carrying out quantitative evaluation of the functions of pumped-storage power stations is an effective means to further play the role of pumped-storage power stations. To this end, this article first analyses the role of pumped-storage power stations in supporting the operation of power system from six aspects: peak-load regulation, energy storage, frequency modulation, phase modulation, reserve, and black start; then, puts forward the principle and calculation method of pumped-storage power station promoting new energy accommodation. Secondly, an evaluation index system for pumped-storage power station supporting power system operation is proposed, and a comprehensive evaluation method for pumped-storage power stations based on analytic hierarchy process is given. Finally, case calculation results based on the actual operating data of the pumped-storage power station verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: ACTIVE DISTRIBUTION NETWORK EXPANSION PLANNING CONSIDERING DEMAND RESPONSE AND NON-COOPERATIVE MULTI-STAKEHOLDER GAME
abstract: The active distribution network (ADN) paradigm has changed the planning and operating scheme of traditional distribution systems. With the development of distributed generation (DG), the power generation business is getting decentralized, and the DG operators (DGOs) and power users are getting more involved in the planning affairs of ADN as independent stakeholders. How to reasonably deploy the network resources according to the needs of different stakeholders whilst satisfying the safe and stable operation of the system is one of the urgent problems to be solved. In this paper, an ADN expansion planning method considering demand response (DR) and non-cooperative game among stakeholders is proposed. Firstly, a DR operator (DRO) model is established, which abstracts the power users as a unified stakeholder; Secondly, a bi-level ADN planning-operating model is established. The upper level model describes the game relation between the distribution network operator (DNO) and the DGOs in the planning layer, and the lower level model describes the game relation between the DNO and the DRO in the operating layer. The genetic algorithm and particle swarm optimization are applied for the solutions of the proposed models. Finally, the case studies are carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Analysis of Power Transmission Limit of Grid-Connected Inverters Based on the Impedance Method
abstract: This paper studies the small-signal stable power transmission limit of the grid-connected inverter based on the impedance method. It is pointed out that when considering the influence of control, the small-signal stable power transmission limit of the grid-connected inverter is smaller than the theoretical power transmission limit. First, the dq-frame impedance model of the grid-connected inverter is derived and verified by simulation measurement. Then the small-signal stable power transmission limit is calculated according to the generalized Nyquist criterion. Finally, the influence of the synchronous reference frame phase-locked loop on the power transmission capacity is analyzed.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional Co-Se-P nanowires network in carbon fiber film for long-cyclic and fast alkali metal ion storage
abstract: Electrode material is a crucial role to improve the performance of alkali metal ion batteries. In this paper, a network of ternary Co-Se-P nanowires grown in carbon fiber membrane is designed to obtain excellent cycling performance and fast storage of lithium/sodium ions. In a ternary nanowire, CoSe nanocrystals are uniformly distributed in amorphous CoP matrix, forming a mutually doped state which can improve the electrical conductivity and electrochemical activity for a high specific capacity even at high current density. Compared with a single Co-Se or P-Co bond, the synergistic effect of multiple chemical bonds improves the structural stability of metal phosphorus selenides, resulting in a highly stable sodiation/desodiation behavior during the long-term cycling. This study provides a new perspective for improving the cyclic stability and rate performance of alkali metal ion anode materials.

articleTitle: FIRST-PRINCIPLES INVESTIGATION OF THE ETL/CsPbIBr2 HETEROJUNCTION: EFFECT OF ELECTRON TRANSPORT LAYER MATERIALS ON INTERFACE PROPERTIES
abstract: With the increase of awareness of environmental protection and the popularization of renewable energy, photovoltaic power generation has been applied in more and more places, and photoelectric conversion materials have gradually become research hotspots. All-inorganic perovskite has become a hotspot in the commercial development of solar cells due to its excellent stability. Although CsPbIBr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> perovskite has excellent stability, serious interface carrier recombination hinders the development of its power conversion efficiency and deteriorates the open circuit voltage. In this work, by studying the ETL/Perovskite interface properties of TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/SnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/ZnO different electron transport layer materials, through the calculation of the electronic properties of the interface and the analysis of the carrier transfer mechanism, the electronic properties of the heterojunction interface are predicted, and an effective theoretical mechanism is provided for experimental research.

articleTitle: Variable-Gain GTSDC to Mitigate SSR in Turbine Generators Connected to Series-Compensated Power Systems
abstract: The generator terminal subsynchronous damping controller (GTSDC) is the considerable option for subsynchronous resonance (SSR) problems in series-compensated transmission systems. However, considering the interaction between the large turbine generator and series compensation system, the transient torque amplification (TA) cannot be effectively suppressed by the GTSDC with a fixed gain due to the deferred-response characteristic, which limits the effectiveness of the conventional GTSDC to mitigate the transient torque when the transmission system failure occurs in the early stage. To address this issue, an improved GTSDC with the variable gain is proposed in this paper, which can rapidly improve the output capacity after the system fault occurs. Firstly, the influence of GTSDC on transient torque is analyzed. Then, the gain tuning is formulated as a constrained optimization problem, in which different operating conditions and disturbances are fully considered secondly. Finally, based on a practical series-compensated transmission system in the Xilin Gol League of China, the effectiveness of the improved GTSDC is verified. The result shows that the proposed GTSDC with variable gain can effectively mitigate the transient torque for the series-compensated transmission system.

articleTitle: AN SSO SOURCE LOCATION METHOD FOR POWER SYSTEMS WITH DFIGS BASED ON HAMILTONIAN SYSTEM THEORY
abstract: Wind farms connected to series-compensated transmission lines have the risk of sub-synchronous oscillation (SSO). The most effective countermeasure against SSOs is to identify the primary cause and then eliminate it. However, it is challenging for existing measurement-based methods to locate SSO sources accurately and timely. To solve this problem, we propose a location method based on the Hamiltonian system theory for identifying the SSO source. Considering the electromagnetic transient process, an energy function for power systems with DFIGs is constructed using the Hamiltonian system theory. The SSO port energy is obtained based on the energy function, and then the SSO source location can be identified by determining the direction of the total SSO port energy flow of a sub-system. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through case studies. The results show that the disturbance source can be located accurately in the forced SSO scenario, and the participation of DFIGs can be evaluated based on the port energy in the negatively damped SSO scenario.

articleTitle: IMPEDANCE STABILITY MARGIN ASSESSMENT FOR WIDEBAND HARMONIC RESONANCES
abstract: The complex hyperbolic functions, which are preserved in the transmission-line model, are the prerequisite of characterizing the propagation deterioration of the wideband harmonic resonances. However, the foresaid functions make it harder to assess the stability margin of the transmission-line systems for the following two reasons: 1) the poles and zeros with finite numbers are difficult to obtain; 2) approximating these functions by the high-order polynomials violates the prerequisites of the imped-ance-based stability criterion. To surmount these impediments, we recommended transforming the hyperbolic functions via Euler’s formula for complex numbers. These transformations enable us to evaluate the applicability of the criterion in terms of the motion patterns of the poles and zeros. We find that: first, due to the distributed parameters, the transmission-line systems are prone to be in critical stability; second, as the frequency increases, the arc-resonance dominant pole fails to cancel the zero periodically, consequently, exciting the resonant peaks; Third, by properly chosen the damping coefficient, not only does the coordinated damper improve the system stability margin, but also it upgrades the cancelation accuracy of the pole and zero.

articleTitle: COORDINATED FREQUENCY SUPPORT AND WIND TURBINE PRESET RESTORATION SCHEME OF VSC-MTDC INTEGRATED OFFSHORE WIND FARMS
abstract: This paper proposes a control scheme for inertial and primary frequency support from voltage source converter-based multi-terminal high-voltage direct current (VSC-MTDC) connected offshore wind farms (OWFs). This scheme consists of the adaptive inertial droop control for onshore stations and the restoration control for offshore wind turbines. On the offshore wind turbine level, each wind turbine adopts adaptive coefficients and provides inertial and primary frequency support by releasing kinetic energy. To address the second frequency drop (SFD) problem and ensure the duration of the frequency support stage, a specific time point is selected to switch from the frequency support stage to the restoration stage through the preset accelerating curve. For onshore VSC stations, the power margin index is used to modify the droop coefficients to avoid over-load accidents and ensure reasonable allocation of frequency support power among onshore stations. Case studies are undertaken on a 3-area 4-terminal VSC-MTDC based offshore wind farms (OWFs). Compared with existing control schemes, the proposed control scheme can improve frequency nadir, reduce SFD, and ensure the transmission power in a safe range. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: STUDY ON THE CHARACTERISTIC ANALYSIS AND FAULT DIAGNOSIS STRATEGY OF ROTOR IMBALANCE OF WIND TURBINE
abstract: The blades of wind turbines may be imbalanced under the terrible environment, and it may cause economic losses and even damage the wind turbine if it cannot be timely identify and dispose .In this paper, characteristics analysis and fault diagnosis research are carried out for rotor imbalance. Firstly, a wind turbine simulation model is set based on GH Bladed , and the signals of different imbalanced conditions are get by setting imbalanced parameters.Secondly, the time-domain characteristics of blade load and tower op load signals under different working conditions and the frequency-domain characteristics of nacelle vibration signal are analyzed.Then, a fault diagnosis model for rotor imbalance of wind turbine is established base on support vector machine (SVM). Finally, the signals of approximate imbalance conditions are used as the training and testing samples.The testing results show that the fault diagnosis model has the ability of reasoning about faults of rotor imbalance.

articleTitle: MPC-BASED ACTIVE POWER COORDINATED CONTROL OF WIND POWER IN SENDING-END POWER GRID
abstract: When the transmission channel fails, there will be the large capacity power surplus in the sending-end power grid with large-scale renewable energy, which leads to the frequency fluctuation of the sending-end power grid, and even affects the safe operation of the sending-end power grid. In this paper, a wind turbines active power coordinated control method based on model predictive control (MPC) is proposed, which can reduce the active power of wind turbine rapidly by increasing the speed of wind turbine. The active power control model based on MPC of wind farm is established. The aim is that the speed of each wind turbine tends to be similar, and the wind turbine with higher speed no longer stores additional kinetic energy. According to the power operation point and rotor speed of wind turbine, the active power coordinated control of wind turbine is realized by reasonably allocating the rising degree of wind turbine rotor speed under different wind speeds, with the constraint of the wind turbine rotor speed not exceeding the limit. The simulation model is established in PowerFactory, and the related algorithm of MPC controller is realized by MATLAB. The simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: A Novel Battery Energy Storage System Based on MMC in HVDC Transmission System
abstract: Modular multilevel converter (MMC) has been verified as a better choice for HVDC, especially in the case of offshore wind power transmission. Battery Energy Storage System Based on MMC (MMC-BESS) can not only deliver power from offshore wind farms, but also smooth the power fluctuations. However, compared with the IGBT rated voltage, the single battery pack has very low rated voltage on the DC side, which leads to very high duty cycle for the DC/DC converter connected with the battery and the SM. In this paper, a novel battery energy storage system based on MMC is proposed, in which a DC/DC converter with high gain ratio is taken. The proposed method ensures availability of the battery pack with low rated voltage, the range of battery pack selection is also expanded. Then, the control strategy is designed to realize the battery power control. Finally, the PSCAD/EMTDC simulations for a HVDC transmission system are conducted to validate the proposed battery integration method and control strategy.

articleTitle: Research on Harmonic Energy Measurement under High Proportion of New Energy Access
abstract: The harmonic content of the power grid formed by a large number of distributed energy is much larger than the traditional power grid, so the traditional power metering scheme is difficult to meet the new demand of new energy grid. This paper analyses the shortcomings of the traditional energy metering scheme in the scenario of power generation and consumption, and proposes an energy metering scheme considering the harmonics of new energy grid. The scheme can realize fundamental energy metering, fundamental power generation metering and harmonic energy metering. Based on the above metering functions, the user compensation and harmonic penalty strategies of the new metering scheme are analysed, and the calculation method of user energy cost under the new metering scheme is given. Finally, through the example analysis, it is proved that the new power metering scheme can ensure the interests of power supply companies and power users.

articleTitle: Selection of Neutral Grounding Resistance for Distribution Networks with Inverter Interfaced Distributed Generation
abstract: Distributed Generation (DG) has been widely used and developed for the integrated use of renewable energy and environmentally friendly energy sources. Most of the DG need to be connected to medium-voltage or low-voltage distribution networks through inverters, which can be called Inverter Interfaced Distributed Generation (IIDG). The large number of accesses to the new power supply makes the distribution network present a double-ended or multi-ended complex network structure. Fault current flow and distribution is changed in turn. Besides, the neutral grounding mode of IIDG grid-connected side transformer affects the fault characteristics as well. When a fault occurs in the distribution network, the fault current provided by IIDG is different from that of traditional generators. According to the operation characteristics of IIDG, the calculation model of short-circuit current under asymmetric fault is established, the detailed theoretical analysis of the system fault electrical quantities under different cases is carried out, and the selection scheme of grounding resistance is further proposed. The digital simulation results of Suzhou example verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis and the practicability of the small resistance value selection scheme.

articleTitle: Review of fully coupled analysis of offshore wind turbine under wind-wave excitation conditions in OC5 project
abstract: Through participating in IEA wind task 30 project of IEA, this review carried out the research on load simulation calculation of offshore wind turbine in OC5 project. During whole project, the bladed for windows is used to establish the hydrodynamic model based on Morison equation and potential flow theory, and the aerodynamic model is established based on blade element momentum theory. The simulation models of monopile model, FOWT model are established. A complete set of modelling method is formed. learn from the valuable experience of OC5 project's experiment design, OC6 project will design a series of scientific experiments, control the uncertainty of the test, separate the key parameters, and cooperate with high-precision CFD calculation, in order to lock the reason of the difference, and really achieve the optimization of the simulation method through experimental correction.

articleTitle: PLL Synchronization Transient Stability Analysis of VSC under Single-Phase-to-Ground AC Fault
abstract: Controlling negative sequence currents at zero is feasible in practice, which can improve the performance of voltage-source converters (VSCs) during asymmetric ac faults. VSCs are usually synchronized with the grid via the phase-locked loop (PLL) However, the synchronization stability is affected by the negative sequence current of VSCs. Hence, this article analyses the PLL transient stability of PLL-synchronized VSCs during single-phase-to-ground ac fault. The parametric impacts of the phase-locked loop and the effect of positive/negative sequence current on synchronization stability are revealed analytically, via employing the phase portrait approach. It is revealed that the loss of synchronization (LOS) possibly arises if VSCs suppress negative sequence current to zero under single-phase-to-ground ac faults. Time-domain simulations are performed in Matlab/Simulink, and the obtained results validate the theoretical findings.

articleTitle: Study on Characteristics of AC/DC Weak Sending System with both Risk of Angle Instability and Transient Overvoltage
abstract: Nowadays with the centralized access of large-capacity high-voltage direct current (HVDC) and high-penetration renewable energy (RE), AC/DC contingencies have brought deep impact on power system operation, which urgently needs further studies. This paper is to study the mechanism of weak sending system with both risk of angle instability and transient overvoltage. Firstly, the characteristic of angle stability considering the impact of wind turbine generators (WTG) was analyzed, and the impact of thermal/wind power output distribution on angle stability was studied. Then, the characteristic of transient overvoltage considering the impact of WTG was analyzed, and the impact of thermal/wind power output distribution on transient overvoltage was also studied. Finally, the interaction between angle stability and transient overvoltage was analyzed, and so was the comprehensive impact on system transmission capability. The study was verified by the simulation results of the practical Ximeng AC/DC weak sending system, which can provide technical references to safe and stable operation of similar electric power systems.

articleTitle: Output Impedance Optimization Method of Cascaded System
abstract: Impedance analysis method is widely used in the field of new energy because of its great engineering application prospect[1-3]. The output impedance of the cascade system will have a peak at the resonant frequency, while the input impedance will have a trough at the resonant frequency[4]. When the input impedance trough overlaps with the output impedance peak, it may cause the oscillation of bus voltage, and then cause the system stability problems[5-6]. Therefore, by optimizing the output impedance, it can avoid the occurrence of impedance overlap, ensure the relative stability of the system, and meet certain performance indicators of the power system[7].

articleTitle: RESEARCH ON TOPOLOGY DESIGN AND CONTROL OF MODULAR MULTILEVEL CONVERTER SUB MODULE
abstract: The DC link fault suppression is a hard technical problem when modular multi-level converter is used in the field of DC transmission system. Because the DC circuit breaker technology is not very mature and the mmanufacturing and operating costs are relatively high, it is still a feasible technical choice to realize DC fault suppression by using sub-module topology. This paper first analyzes the common problems of various self-blocking sub module topologies and their hybrid topologies. Then, the composited sub module topology is designed based on the monopole full bridge topology and multilevel capacitor energy storage network. This paper further analyzes the DC fault suppression characteristics of the composited sub module topology under different blocking modes, and studies the unbalanced capacitor charging problem of the sub module in the fault blocking stage and its countermeasures. At the same time, aiming at the problem of capacitor voltage divergence caused by long-term blocking, a non-blocking fault control strategy is designed. Finally, a simulation model is built in PSCAD / EMTDC to verify the DC fault suppression characteristics and control strategy of the composited topology.

articleTitle: Detection of Close Frequency Voltage Fluctuations Using Equal Interval Analytic Mode Decomposition
abstract: Voltage fluctuations get the attention of people more and more since they harm on electrical equipment seriously. Close frequency voltage fluctuations (CFVFs) are caused by a set of sources or loads which have similar transmissive power, installation positions, and cyclical work. The detected methods of CFVFs are affected by the close degree of frequencies and sampling time. The paper is based on analytical mode decomposition (AMD) that can be as a filter to realize effective detection of CFVFs. First, in order to improve the applicability of AMD, the detection method of equal interval AMD (EIAMD) is presented. Second, the filter performance and its improvement influenced by ending effect are discussed, and the detection flow is obtained. Finally, the correctness of theoretical findings is substantiated by simulation results.

articleTitle: TRANSIENT STABILITY OF LOW-INERTIA POWER GRID WITH INVERTER-BASED GENERATIONS
abstract: This paper aims to investigate the transient stability of the low-inertia power grid with integration of large-scale phase-locked loop (PLL)-driven inverter-based generations (IBGs). An equivalent second-order motion-equation model of the low-inertia power grid is developed to describe the synchronization behaviour between the IBG and the traditional SG. The concept of equivalent inertia ratio of the power grid is firstly proposed as the key index to evaluate the transient stability of the system. It is found that severe fault depth and small equivalent inertia ratio of the system will deteriorate the transient stability. The voltage at the point of the common coupling (PCC), as the input of PLL, is more easily disturbed under severe fault, which may destabilize the system. The small equivalent inertia ratio of the system slows down the PLL’s synchronization speed to the SG and leads to poor transient stability. This paper contributes to understanding the mechanism of the interaction between the PLL and the SG in the low-inertia grid. The analysis is verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Real-Time Optimal Economic Dispatch of Active Distribution Network Considering Energy Storage and Distributed Generation Integration
abstract: This paper proposes an active distribution network (ADN) real-time optimal economic dispatch model. The model has been reformulated and generalized while still retaining a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) problem representation, which is able to find a stable global minimum of the objective function. Careful attention is paid to the appropriate scaling of this optimization for operating periods under real-time conditions. The real-time optimization model is calculated every 5 minutes within a rolling horizon of 1 hour. The distributed energy resources (DERs) include dispatchable gas turbines, distributed PV stations, wind farms, and energy storage systems. The cost functions of gas turbines are approximated via piecewise linearization and all the technical parameters are considered in the model. The distributed solar and wind have their real-time power prediction of the next time period as boundary conditions. Also, both energy storage and load-serving entities are permitted to submit price-sensitive demand bids. The total ADN needs to fulfill node power balance and line flow constraints. The simulation results demonstrate the validity of the optimization model as well as the benefits of reducing ADN's total operation cost and maximizing the users' benefit.

articleTitle: THE OPTIMAL DISPATCH OF MOBILE ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEM FOR THE BLACK-START OF TRADITIONAL THERMAL GENERATORS
abstract: The amount of black-start (BS) units is the key factor affecting system restoration efficiency after blackouts. The existing studies mainly use the hydropower units with self-starting ability as the BS generators. However, the lack of hydropower units is common in most of provincial power gird, which makes the system restoration efficiency hard to improve. An efficient method to improve the restoration efficiency is to increase the number of BS generators. With the deployment of flexible dispatching mobile energy storage systems (MESSs) in power system, they can provide power support for the BS of traditional thermal power units. Therefore, the optimal dispatch method of MESSs is proposed in this paper to re-energize traditional thermal generators for improving the restoration efficiency of power system. This paper utilizes spectral clustering algorithm to separate the affected power system into several subsystems and obtain sectionalizing result, which is used to optimize the dispatch of MESSs and determine the location of BS units. The restoration efficiency is finally improved by restoring the created subsystems in parallel. The New England 10-unit 39-bus power system is employed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method for large-scale networks.

articleTitle: Physical Model Induced Neural Network for Wind Speed Prediction for Wind Turbines under Wake Effects
abstract: Wake effect is one of the main factors to cause power losses of wind farm. Accurate prediction of inflow wind speeds of wind turbines under wake effects is difficult while is important for its precise output power prediction. This paper proposed four physical model induced machine learning algorithms for wind speed prediction of wind turbines under wake effects. The four algorithms are hybrid physics-and-neural network models, which include hybrid-physics-data based neural network model, physical model based data transfer learning model, physical model regularization model and hybrid model of physical model and weighted neural network network. The predicted wind speeds using these four models are compared to actual SCADA data from a wind farm in northern Jiangsu, China. The prediction accuracy is analysed and the pros and cons of the four models are compared. Their generalization capabilities of wind speed prediction are further evaluated. It is found that compared to pure neural network, improved prediction accuracies of wind speeds are obtained. The results show superior performance of hybrid physics-and-neural network models for wind speed prediction. It provides a feasible way to predict wind turbine power output considering wake effects, which is meaningful for wind farm wake control.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation of PSS performance in the AC-DC grid for small disturbance stability
abstract: The access of the AC-DC grid changes the stable form and operation characteristics of the power grid. The dynamic regulation of the excitation system of a large synchronous generator still has a great influence on the stability of the power system. Proper excitation setting can increase the system damping and quickly respond to the regulation demand for stability. This paper talks about the modeling and simulation of the PSS in excitation system for small signal stability of the power system. Firstly, the source-network equivalent model is established, which is an extension of the traditional synchronous generator electromechanical transient model combined with a multi-machine system and VSC access analysis. The correctness is verified by the field test data, and then the effect of PSS on the system stability is discussed in the case of multi-machine power system and AC-DC hybrid system. Finally, the detailed electromagnetic transient model of AC-DC hybrid grid is built in PSCAD, and the performance of PSS is simulated and tested again. The results show the effectiveness of the proposed model and the importance of the PSS parameter should be well-tuned.

articleTitle: Research on control strategy of canceling tap changer in back to back DC project
abstract: UHVDC project and back-to-back HVDC project, as the main ways of clean energy consumption, will play an increasingly important role in the future. At present, the Fujian Guangdong interconnection project has been approved. After the completion of the Fujian Guangdong interconnection project, the interconnection of Fujian and Guangdong power grids will be realized, which has important demonstration significance for building a clean, low-carbon, safe and efficient energy system and ensuring regional energy security.This paper first analyzes the conventional control strategy of back-to-back project, then calculates the main circuit parameters after the tap changer is cancelled, studies the control strategy of back-to-back DC project, and builds PSCAD model to simulate and analyze various working conditions.
