The research results show that the corresponding control strategy can meet the requirements of stable operation of DC system.

articleTitle: Reliability Evaluation Method of Fusion Station under Multi-Station Integration Mode
abstract: Substation, data center, energy storage station, renewable energy generation station and other resources are integrated to form a fusion station under multi-station integration mode. This kind of fusion station with data center has high demand for power supply reliability. At present, there are few researches on power supply reliability evaluation of fusion station, and the existing researches mostly use reliability block diagram to analyze. However, it is difficult to analyze the influence caused by the fluctuation of renewable energy and charging and discharging strategy of energy storage station by using reliability block diagram. In this paper, a reliability evaluation method based on signal simulation is proposed. Firstly, a simulation model which can simulate the power flow during the operation of the fusion station is established based on the characteristics of each device. Then through Monte Carlo method and operation simulation, the power supply reliability can be obtained. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by a typical example.

articleTitle: STABILITY ANALYSIS METHOD OF WIND INTEGRATED POWER SYSTEM BASED ON REDUCED-ORDER ADMITTANCE MODEL IN SUB-BANDS
abstract: Power system with high penetration of wind generation contains a number of devices with complex external characteristics such as converters. Due to the high order of the admittance model, it may be difficult to analyse the system stability directly by zeroes of the determinant of the admittance matrix. To fill this gap, a zeros identification method based on a reduced-order admittance model in sub-bands was proposed in this paper. It divides the frequency band to be investigated into several sub-bands. In each sub-band, only the dominant oscillation mode is retained and the frequency response of other terms is equivalent by a unified exponential expression. Hence, a simplified reduced-order equivalent model of the admittance is established. The parameters of the reduced-order model can be obtained by fitting algorithms, and then zeros of the reduced-order model in each sub-band can be solved to access the system stability. The proposed method significantly reduces the difficulty of stability analysis, particularly for high-order systems. Both eigenvalue analysis and time-domain simulations have been presented in the case study to validate its effectiveness and accuracy.

articleTitle: DC Bus Voltage Control for a DC Microgrid with Hydrogen Storage Based on ESO and Terminal Sliding Mode Control
abstract: DC microgrid can accept distributed energy more efficiently and realize complementary advantages between each distributed power source. The voltage stability of DC bus is an important index to measure the stability of the system, so suppressing the voltage fluctuations is an important goal of the stability control of DC microgrid. In order to suppress the impacts of the dc bus voltage, this paper proposed an effective strategy for a nonlinear robust current feed forward control which consists of terminal sliding mode control and extended state observer (ESO), based on the traditional voltage and current closed-loop control strategy. ESO is used to quickly track system states and the uncertainties and disturbances of the system, and realize the fast suppression of the transient bus voltage fluctuation in the system. In addition, the electrolytic cell, as a controllable load, was considered to participate in the regulation of DC bus voltage. By modeling the electrolytic cell and using the response characteristics of the controllable load, the fuel cell and electrolytic cell are coordinated to complete the stable control of distribution network voltage. The effectiveness of the proposed voltage fluctuation suppression strategy was verified by using DIgSILENT simulation software to build a DC micro-grid system.

articleTitle: Frequency Control Strategy of Wind Turbines Based on Reduced-order Frequency Response Model
abstract: For the power system with multiple types of frequency regulation resources such as thermal power, hydropower and new energy frequency control, the frequency dynamics under disturbance are extremely complex. The low order model considering only single resource is insufficient, while the high order model is not conducive to the analytical calculation of key frequency indexes, that is, a reduced-order model which can describe the frequency dynamics of multiple resources is needed. In this paper, the dominant pole reduction method is used to reduce the order of complex frequency models, and derive the analytical expressions of frequency indexes. On this basis, the root locus method is used to analyze the influence of wind turbines frequency control on system stability. At the same time, the frequency control parameters of wind turbine are set taken account to frequency constraints and dynamic stability. At last, the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method are verified by simulation, which provide a basis for analyzing the frequency dynamics and improving system dynamic stability.

articleTitle: Research on Early Warning of Continuous Commutation Failure of HVDC Transmission Line Based on Machine Learning Methods
abstract: High-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission systems have developed rapidly in recent years. Continuous commutation failure is a serious malfunction in HVDC transmission systems, which results in the blockage of the converter station. Though commutation failure is inevitable when serious AC side faults occur, continuous commutation failure can be prevented by control methods based on a sensitive and accurate forecast. However, the HVDC transmission systems are complex and nonlinear when commutation failure occurs. Thus, analytical methods are limited. Hence, a new forecasting method based on machine learning is introduced. First, this paper analyses the physical process of commutation failures. Commutation voltage, direct current, and advancing firing angle are the main factors that affect the commutation failure of HVDC. Second, this paper realizes the training and evaluation of the continuous commutation failure classification and probabilistic forecasting model. Data processing and feature engineering methods have significantly improved the model performance. Finally, the proposed model is tested on the CIGRE benchmark system. The proposed model can predict whether a continuous commutation failure will occur within tens of milliseconds after the first commutation failure, where the risk of continuous commutation failure is greatly reduced.

articleTitle: RESEARCH ON PARTIAL DISCHARGE CHARACTERISTICS OF 500KV OIL-IMMERSED INVERTED CURRENT TRANSFORMER UNDER IMPULSE VOLTAGE
abstract: Oil-immersed current transformers are susceptible to partial discharge due to lightning and switching impulse voltage during operation. Continuous discharge will cause damage to the equipment insulation. In this paper, a partial discharge test circuit under impulse voltage for 500kV oil-immersed inverted current transformer was built. By applying standard lightning and switching impulse voltage to the equipment, partial discharge signals are collected by non-contact high-frequency partial discharge sensors. And various insulation tests after the impulse test were carried out. The results show that partial discharge will appear in the oil-immersed current transformer during the impulse voltage. The partial discharge extinguishing voltage is lower than the operating voltage, which means the discharge cannot be self-extinguished. Long-term cumulative effects can cause equipment failure.

articleTitle: MULTI-OBJECTIVE OPTIMAL SCHEDULING OF MICROGRID CONSIDERING DISTRIBUTED GENERATION UNCERTAINTY
abstract: With the continuous increase of distributed wind power/photovoltaic (PV) grid-connected capacity, the uncertainties of wind and PV power outputs have brought new problems and severe challenges to the day-ahead optimal scheduling of microgrids. Based on the forecasting error information of distributed wind/PV power output and peak-valley time-of-use electricity price mechanism, from the perspective of meeting the load demand of the microgrid, this paper proposes a dual-objective optimization model that minimizes the operation cost of the microgrid and maximizes the wind/PV power accommodation rate subject to a series of system constraints. The established optimization model comprehensively takes the maintenance costs of wind turbine and PV, the costs of battery charging and discharging, and the cost of energy exchange with the main grid into account. The proposed optimization model is solved by a multi-objective feasibility enhanced particle swarm optimization algorithm to realize the optimization of the output of distributed generation, the interaction of microgrid and main grid energy, and the all-day energy management scheme of the energy storage system. Finally, the numerical simulations are performed on a microgrid test system to verify the effectiveness of the proposed model and scheduling strategy.

articleTitle: A Protection Scheme Based on the Current-limiting Reactor Voltage and its Derivation for MMC-MVDC
abstract: High-speed and reliable protection is the key to ensure safe operation of DC network. This paper raises a protection scheme based on the current-limiting reactor voltage and its derivation for MMC-MVDC. By analyzing the fault characteristics of MMC-MVDC network, a pick-up criterion based on the reactor voltage is proposed. Based on the different derivation of reactor voltage for pole-to-pole fault, and the different polarity of reactor voltage of two poles between internal and external fault, the protection criteria for internal-external distinguish are put forward. Using the variation of line voltage, the criterion of fault pole selection is realized. The proposed scheme is verified by a four-terminal DC network model. The operation conditions include different fault types, internal and external fault and various fault resistance are considered. The simulation results show that the proposed scheme can selectively and speedily remove all internal faults and it also has a good ability to overcome the effect of fault resistance.

articleTitle: RISK ASSESSMENT OF SUBSTATIONS IN A CYBERPHYSICAL POWER SYSTEM CONSIDERING ATTACKER'S INTRUSION BEHAVIOR
abstract: In the cyber-physical power system, a powerful cyber network is built to transmit data information and orders between the substations and the control centre, which also means expert attackers can easily break into the hosts once they obtain the access to the cyber network of power system. In this situation, the attacker can choose an attack path targeting a more influential substation with lower difficulty and higher concealment. In this paper, a risk assessment model is developed by introducing attack graph which considers the success probability of attacker's intrusion behavior on the cyber side. This model evaluates the cybersecurity vulnerability of substations by analysing the technical difficulty of potential cyber-attack paths, and the load loss of the physical system under N-2 contingency is calculated by an optimal model based on DC load flow. According to the vulnerability analysis on the cyber side and the corresponding attack impact analysis on the physical side, the critical substations in CPPS can be identified, which provides a reference for defender in distributing defence resource and mitigating load loss caused by attacks. Finally, the case studies are performed on the IEEE-30 bus system to demonstrate the validity of the proposed risk assessment model.

articleTitle: THE INTEGRATION OF RENEWABLE GENERATION WITH ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING
abstract:
There are three major developments that are having a significant impact on power system operation and development;

Meeting the requirement to decarbonise electricity generation;

Accommodating increasing volumes of non-synchronous renewable generation;

Accommodating supplies for electric vehicle charging and domestic heat pumps.

 This paper discusses these developments, quantifies their impact and defines an optimum approach to managing their integration to minimise the costs to consumers and disruption to the sector. The focus is to advance the concept of linking the intermittent output from increasing levels of generation like wind and solar to the charging infrastructure for the evolving tranche of electric vehicles and heating. It is shown how a significant reduction can be realised in future generation capacity requirements and costs to end users.

articleTitle: Real-Time Scheduling Method Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning for a Hybrid Wind-Solar-Storage Energy Generation System
abstract: With the large-scale penetration of renewable energy in recent years, the volatility and randomness have posed huge challenges to the optimal operation of the power systems. Meanwhile, because of the model uncertainty, parameter uncertainty and time coupling, it is very difficult to develop an universal real-time energy scheduling method for various situations. To cope with the challenges, this paper proposes a novel real-time scheduling method for a hybrid wind-solar-storage energy generation system. The real-time scheduling problem is firstly formulated as a Markov decision process (MDP), and then a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method based on deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm is proposed to solve this problem. Different from the traditional model-based methods, the proposed method is model-free and does not need to know or forecast the uncertain information (e.g., renewable energy generation, electricity demand, etc.). The proposed method can learn from a large amount of past data to make optimal decisions. Finally, simulation results based on various scenarios verify the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving renewable energy consumption, reducing the total generation cost, and smoothing power fluctuation, etc.

articleTitle: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF IMPACT OF WIND FARM SIDE MMC WITH DIFFERENT AC VOLTAGE CONTROL STRATEGIES ON THE STABILITY OF MMC-HVDC CONNECTED WIND FARM
abstract: The modular multilevel converter based high-voltage dc (MMC-HVDC) transmission has been the preferred scheme for power transfer of offshore wind farms that are far away from coastline. For the wind farm side MMC (WFMMC), its main control target is to produce and maintain the ac voltage at the interconnection point of the wind farm and HVDC system. However, interactive oscillations between the wind farm and WFMMC may happen, which have been observed in several practical systems in recent years. In this paper, the impacts of three kinds of ac voltage control strategies of the WFMMC on the stability of the wind farm-MMC interconnected system will be analysed. To do that, the detailed broadband impedance models of the WFMMC with different ac voltage control strategies are established, respectively, which are verified by measured impedances in simulation. Then, the comparative analysis of the impedance characteristics of the WFMMC with different control strategies is carried out and the stability of the interconnected system is then analysed under different power conditions using impedance-based method. The results show that different ac voltage control strategies have great impact on the ac-side impedance characteristics of the WFMMC as well as on the stability of the interconnected system.

articleTitle: Research on Task Unloading Algorithm Based on Edge Terminal Server of Power Distribution Station Area
abstract: Edge terminal server is one of the important devices for cloud edge collaboration in the future power distribution station area. With the increasing business of the power distribution station area, it needs to process a large amount of user data quickly and efficiently. As a result, it is more and more sensitive to power consumption and task delay, which poses a severe challenge to edge terminal server. To solve this problem, a task unloading algorithm based on edge terminal server is proposed. Firstly, a directed acyclic graph is constructed according to the distribution characteristics of the edge terminal server in the power distribution station area, and the complete parallelism between the edge terminal server and the equipment in the power distribution station area is established. Then, the task offloading is described as a joint optimization problem to minimize the energy consumption and task delay, and a heuristic intelligent algorithm is proposed to ensure the dependencies between subtasks and improve the task efficiency. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified through the Matlab/simulink simulation results.

articleTitle: Matching-Control of Wind Power System Based on Current Source Converter
abstract: The weak grid lacks frequency support capability and may cause the broadband oscillation because of the coupling of the traditional vector control loop of current and the phase-locked-loop (PLL). To solve this issue, this paper presents a new method applied to the permanent magnetic synchronous generator (PMSG)-based wind power converter which is based on current source converter (CSC) and is called “Matching-Control”. In contrast to the conventional PLL-based synchronization method, the Matching-Control makes the grid side converter (GSC) realize self-synchronization by adopting the intrinsic dynamics of the DC-link inductor so the PLL could be removed and there will be no coupling problem of those control loops. An additional inertia transmission control loop is added to the machine-side control loop to improve the inertial response ability after receiving the frequency information transferred by the GSC and then utilizes the kinetic stored in the rotor of wind turbines to support the recovery of the grid. Therefore, under the Matching-Control, wind power converters show the characteristics of a synchronous generator and needs no PLL to keep synchronization with the power grid. Finally, on the Simulink/MATLAB simulation platform, the feasibility of the proposed method and the correctness of the theoretical analysis are verified.

articleTitle: Study on PCS Topology of Large Capacity Energy Storage System Based on Retired Power Battery Reuse
abstract: With the rapid growth of production and marketing of electric vehicles (EVs) worldwide, and with the increasing number of EV batteries failing to output original energy, a large number of EV batteries will gradually be retired. Although the retired EV batteries are not suitable for continuous use in their first-life scenarios because of capacity attenuation, they can still meet the requirements of energy storage applications in power grid. Compared with other existing ways of reusing retired EV batteries, the way of direct use without disassembling the battery pack is more cost-effective, safe and reliable. In this paper, based on the characteristics of retired EV battery pack, the several kinds of power conversion system (PCS) topologies in large capacity battery energy storage system (BESS) is analyzed and compared. Then a new PCS scheme, in which multi-branch DC/DC paralleled with DC/AC as a module unit, and multi-unit AC side in paralleled, is proposed. Finally, using the whole pack utilization way of retired EV batteries, the proposed PCS scheme is designed and applied in a large capacity BESS project in an industrial park in Shenzhen.

articleTitle: Spatial-Temporal Graph Neural Network for Regional Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Based on Weather Condition Recognition
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power generation can effectively utilize solar energy resources. The regional PV power forecasting is helpful for dispatchers to formulate dispatching plans in a more scientific and reasonable way. At present, the existing methods don't sufficiently consider the temporal correlation of power output and the physical connection caused by clouds movement between PV plants. Aiming at these shortcomings, this paper proposes a spatial-temporal graph neural network method for regional photovoltaic power forecasting based on weather condition recognition. Firstly, we select the spatial-temporal graph convolutional neural network as the forecasting model, which can capture spatial feature through the Graph Convolution Neural model and capture temporal feature through the Gated Convolution Neural unit. The input is the graph structure data consists of the feature matrix and the adjacency matrix representing the connection relationship between plants, the output is the regional power. Secondly, due to the correlations between PV plants varies with weather conditions, we divide the weather into three categories: cloudless, partial cloud coverage and total cloud coverage. Different adjacency matrices will set for different weather conditions to train the forecasting model. Finally, the actual operation data is used for simulation, and the results verify the effectiveness of classification forecasting.

articleTitle: DEVEIOPMENT PROSPECTS OF HIGH ECONOMY XLPE INSULATION HVDC SUBMARINE CABLE
abstract: The material consumables of HVDC submarine cable required per unit transmission capacity was taken as a typical economic index, based on that, the economy of HVDC submarine cable was improved both with voltage and current capacity increasing for a single HVDC submarine cable circuit. Compared the material consumables with the increase of voltage and the current capacity of HVDC submarine cable based on different routes, it was cleared that the improvement of voltage and current capacity respectively by increasing the Insulation tolerance level and the maximum operating temperature of conductor is more effective in improving the economy of HVDC submarine cable. In addition, ±525kV DC submarine cable was selected as a typical specification, whose insulation field strength distribution was analyzed through finite element simulation after the applied voltage was increased to 972kV and the conductor operating temperature was increased from 70°C to 90°C. The results showed that the increase of applied voltage and conductor operating temperature would both caused a further increase of the field strength close to the insulation shield after the insulation field strength reversal, and there is an additional synergism between voltage and temperature.

articleTitle: Multi-time Scale Collaborative Optimal Dispatching for Regional Grid Integrated with Renewable Energy and Battery Energy Storage Based on GrowNet
abstract: With the development of renewable energy, Battery Energy Storage (BESS) has great potential in reducing the negative impact of renewable energy to modern power grid. In this paper, a forecasting framework based on gradient boosting neural network (GrowNet) is proposed, which can build a hierarchical deep neural network prediction model for the renewable energy. And a multi-time scale optimal dispatching framework based on improved model predictive control (MPC) is built for the system integrated with renewable energy and BESS, not only realizes the goal of lowest composite cost in day-ahead phase, but also reduces the fluctuation of tie-line power and the state of charge (SOC) of BESS, and tracks the planned power generation of renewable energy in intra-day phase. An improved genetic algorithm (GA) is used to solve the day-ahead optimal dispatching model, and the intra-day rolling optimal dispatching model is solved by quadratic programming combined with MPC. The simulation results show that the composite framework of forecasting and dispatching is practical and can achieve multiple optimization objectives.

articleTitle: HIGH-FREQUENCY IMPEDANCE MODEL OF MODULAR MULTILEVEL CONVERTER FOR HIGHFREQUENCY RESONANCE ANALYSIS
abstract: The high-voltage dc (HVDC) transmission is preferred for grid-integration of large-scale long-distance offshore wind farms and practical projects based on the modular multilevel converter (MMC) for wind farms have been globally put into operation or under construction. However, the high-frequency resonance (HFR) phenomena have frequently happened in the MMCHVDC projects in recent years, e.g., 1271 Hz HFR in LuXi Project, 700 Hz and 1.8 kHz HFR in YuE Project, etc. To reveal the generation mechanisms of the HFR phenomena, a simple but accurate model is necessary. Nevertheless, the existing models of MMC are either too complicated or overly simplified, which are not appropriate to the HFR analysis. In this paper, an accurate high-frequency impedance model of MMC is proposed for the HFR analysis. The island control and gridconnection control of MMC are considered in the modelling, respectively. The developed high-frequency impedance models are compared with the detailed impedance models of MMC with different control strategies, which shows that the highfrequency impedance models are able to accurately represent all the impedance characteristics in the high-frequency range above 200 Hz. Furthermore, the impact of different control strategies on the high-frequency impedance characteristics is discussed.

articleTitle: AN EQUIPMENT-ORIENTED VULNERABILITY THREAT ASSESSMENT METHOD FOR ELECTRIC POWER SUPERVISION AND CONTROL SYSTEMS
abstract: With increasing application of information technology in supervision and control of power systems, the risk of cyber-attacks in power grids continues to rise. Organized and premeditated cyber attacks have become prominent security threat to power systems. Vulnerability index is used to describe security degree of a computer controling system, so can be used in power systems, which can be regarded as distributed computer controling systems. This paper proposes a method to assess vulnerability threat of key equipments in electric power supervision and control systems. Considering system configuration and hackers' attack skills, an evaluation model of cyber attack behaviors based on analytic hierarchy process is built firstly. Then a probability model is established to evaluate the probability of each attack path consisting of multi behaviors. Finally, an equipment-oriented vulnerability threat assessment method is proposed, using cyber attack behavior evaluation results and probability of related attack path as iput. The method considers both system configuration conditions and hackers' attack skill evaluation, and realizes quantitative evaluation of vulnerability threat of key equipments. An IEC 61850 based substation system is analyzed as test case, to verify the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: ANALYSIS OF NEW STABILITY CHARACTERISTICS OF LARGE-SCALE RENEWABLE ENERGY CONNECTED TO POWER SYSTEM
abstract: Driven by the goal of “Carbon Neutral and Carbon Peak”, the large-scale application of renewable energy has become the inevitable trend of power system development in China. With the rapid development of renewable energy, the stability characteristics of the traditional power systems will change greatly. Under the scene of large-scale renewable energy access in Northwest power grid, and based on the existing structure of Northwest power grid, this paper simulates the development trend of renewable energy in the future, and builds different thermal electricity output scenarios and different renewable energy proportion scenarios by PSD-BPA. In these proposed scenarios, the synchronization stability, voltage stability, and frequency stability of the power system are simulated and analyzed. According to the result of the simulation, the new stability characteristics of the Northwest power grid with high penetration of renewable energy resources are extracted and the influence mechanism of the renewable energy access percentage on power stability is analyzed.

articleTitle: Accurate linearized models for Saturated Transformer of LCC-HVDC under Two Types of DC-Biased Currents
abstract: This paper derives accurate linearized models for saturated transformer of line commutated converter based high voltage direct current (LCC-HVDC) transmission system under two types of DC-biased currents. Firstly, the linearized model of saturated single-phase transformer is theoretically elaborated by a simplified nonlinear magnetic curve. Developing the analyzed method for single-phase transformer to three-phase transformer, the linearized models for saturated three-phase transformer under two types of DC-biased currents are mathematically derived. Furthermore, by circulation path analyzing, the DC-biased harmonic instability of LCC-HVDC can be triggered by converter modulated DC-biased current also is systematically analyzed. The simulation tests by PSCAD/EMTDC are performed to verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis. The consistency between the simulation results and theoretical analysis verifies the effectiveness of the proposed theory.

articleTitle: AN ADAPTIVE WIDEBAND OSCILLATION SUPPRESSION METHOD FOR WIND FARM INTEGRATION THROUGH MMC-HVDC SYSTEM
abstract: With the rapid development of modular multilevel converter-based high-voltage DC (MMC-HVDC) transmission system for wind farm integration, the wideband oscillation issues have become increasingly serious. By far, most of the oscillation suppression methods are merely suitable for oscillation suppression in a specific frequency range, e.g., sub-/super-synchronous oscillation and high-frequency oscillation. In this paper, an adaptive wideband oscillation suppression method for wind farm integration through MMC-HVDC system is proposed in order to mitigate various oscillations adaptively. The wideband impedance models of the wind farm and MMC are derived analytically, which are validated by frequency scanning in simulation. Then, the effect of the proposed oscillation suppression method is theoretically analysed based on the impedance-frequency characteristics. The time-domain simulation model of wind farm integration through MMC-HVDC system is built in MATLAB/Simulink. Two oscillatory cases, i.e., sub-/super-synchronous oscillation and high-frequency oscillation, are carried out to validate the effectiveness of the proposed adaptive wideband oscillation suppression method. It is worth noting that the proposed oscillation suppression method can be applied in both controllers of wind turbine converters and wind farm side MMC.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Evaluation Model of Microgrid's Renewable Energy Consumption Ability Based on Fuzzy Theory
abstract: The development of microgrids is an effective way to solve large-scale distributed renewable energy consumption, smooth the impact of randomness and volatility caused by their output nature on the grid. Most of the existing works evaluate the microgrid system from the perspective of economic benefits, and there is no mature evaluation system for the renewable energy consumption capacity of the microgrid. The establishment of a comprehensive assessment system of renewable energy consumption capacity of microgrids is important for the construction and development of it. This article first explores and analyzes the influencing indexes of the renewable energy consumption capacity in the microgrid, further establishes the evaluation system, and proposes a combined weighting method based on AHP and CRITIC to weight the evaluation indexes. Finally, the improved fuzzy evaluation is used for comprehensive evaluation. In addition, a comprehensive evaluation of microgrids in three different scenarios was carried out. The results obtained are reasonable and can be used for engineering practice and reference.

articleTitle: A Data-driven Active Distribution Network Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Random Matrix Theory
abstract: With the rapid expansion of distribution network and the access of a large number of distributed generators (DG), the traditional fault diagnosis method is no longer applicable to the current active distribution network due to its excessive dependence on mechanism models and restricted application conditions. This paper proposes a data-driven method for fault diagnosis based on random matrix theory. A high dimension matrix model which consists of voltage measurement data of each node is built. The characteristics of eigenvalue distribution are obtained according to the ring law theorem. The mean spectral radius (MSR) is selected as the linear eigenvalue statistic to determine the moment of fault occurrence. For fault location, the augment matrix theory is applied for data correlation analysis, and the MSR deviation rate is constructed as the quantitative indicator to measure the influence degree of each node's voltage on the operating state of the system. Finally, simulations are implemented on IEEE-33 model to verify the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method. The article realizes fault identification and location merely relying on the statistical property analysis with favourable accuracy and robustness to normal fluctuations, which is not affected by the structure and scale of distribution network.

articleTitle: EXTRACTION AND ANALYSIS OF KEY INFLUENCING FACTORS OF DAMPING CHARACTERISTICS OF MODULAR MULTILEVEL CONVERTER
abstract: The modular multilevel converter based high voltage dc (MMC-HVDC) transmission has been widely used in grid-integration of large-scale renewable power plants, especially for offshore wind farms. However, the sub/super-synchronous oscillation (SSO) and high-frequency resonance (HFR) phenomena have been reported in many MMC-HVDC projects during the last decade. To reveal the generation mechanisms of these oscillatory phenomena, the accurate ac-side impedance model of MMC is established based on harmonic state space (HSS) method in this paper, which includes all control loops and internal dynamics within MMC. The analytical impedance model is validated by frequency scanning in simulation. Based on the impedance model, a damping characteristics analysis method is proposed to extract and analyse the key influencing factors on the damping characteristics of MMC. To do that, a damping sensitivity of different parameters in main circuit and controller is defined to quantitatively assess and extract the key factors that mainly influence the damping characteristics in different frequency ranges. Subsequently, how those key factors influence the damping characteristics in different frequency ranges is then analysed using three-dimensional diagrams. Finally, the simulation results have confirmed the above theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Research on Distribution Network Harmonic Source and Weak Points Identification Based on Data Association Analysis
abstract: In the current power grid, new energy sources and non-linear loads lead to higher harmonics, making the power grid vulnerable to security and stability. This article uses the data association analysis FP-growth algorithm to track the harmonic source and week points in the distribution network. By analyzing the actual power quality data, the harmonic correlation of each monitoring node is analyzed. Frequent itemsets of monitoring nodes with high relevance in each harmonic are searched. According to the harmonic sequence relationship of each monitoring node, the proportion of the harmonic power injected by each monitoring node and monitoring node combination is calculated. The harmonic source is judge by forming theprobability function for each monitoring node. Simulations based on actual power quality data are conducted to obtain the harmonic sequence relationship and to judge the harmonic source. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified.

articleTitle: Coordinated Strategy of Multi-Aggregator in Spot Market Under Uncertainty: A Stochastic and Robust Optimization Approach
abstract: This paper proposes a coordinated strategy of multi-aggregators in day-ahead and real-time markets. Aggregators consist of various intermittent renewable energy, electric vehicle aggregator and energy storage systems. The coordinated operation of multi-aggregators are confronted with challenging due to the uncertainties, involved in the production of intermittent renewable energy, the market prices and the characteristic of the loads. In order to solve the forehead problem, a hierarchical zonal framework and a two-stage stochastic robust optimization model is proposed for coordinated bidding strategy of multi-aggregators under uncertainties. In this proposed method, the uncertain day-ahead market prices are depicted by different stochastic scenarios, while a robust optimization by confidence bounds is modeled the real-time market prices, the output of the intermittent renewable energy and characteristic of the electric vehicle are modeled, with multi-aggregators behaving as a price-taker in the market. Numerical simulations illustrate the advantage of the proposed approach in terms of reasonableness and effectiveness in computational efficiency and the scheduling cost reducing.

articleTitle: Analysis Method for Complementarity of Wind-Solar-Hydro Power Outputs Based on Improved Spectral Clustering
abstract: To overcome the shortcomings of wind-solar-hydro hybrid generation system that different energy sources have greatly different data features and complex fluctuation characteristics, a complementarity analysis method for wind-solar-hydro power outputs based on the improved spectral clustering is proposed. To begin with, the theoretical outputs of wind, solar and hydro power is calculated based on meteorological data. Then, in accordance with NJW algorithm and the simultaneous backward reduction algorithm based on the Kantorovich distance (KD algorithm), an improved spectral clustering algorithm is proposed to screen the typical days of wind-solar-hydro power outputs, and the clustering validity of it is verified by indices calculation. Finally, the complementarity of wind-solar-hydro power outputs on typical days is quantitatively analyzed from two perspectives of fluctuation and ramp. The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm has better clustering quality than NJW algorithm, K-means and KD algorithm, which can be used to select typical days of wind-solar-hydro power outputs. It is also found that the combined generation can improve the volatility of power outputs and the offset effect on the ramp events is higher than the random fluctuation. This work will provide reference for the capacity allocation and optimal scheduling of combined power stations.

articleTitle: Battery Energy Storage System Allocation for Reliability Optimization of Distribution Network
abstract: Reliability is one of the key aspects in the design and operation of power distribution network (PDN). Battery energy storage system (BESS) is used to improve reliability of the PDN. Traditional method of configuring BESS in distribution network is based on software that uses the concept of brute force in systems analysis. Besides, efficiency of configuring BESS is not considered. In this paper, a novel method for allocating BESS is proposed, which improves the system's reliability and gets maximum cost-benefit ratio. Compared with traditional method, the allocation plan of BESS is presented by using the proposed method is more explicate and easier. The proposed method is based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) and takes both the cost of configuring BESS and the income of the reliability improvement into consideration. Firstly, the proposed PSO-based method for optimizing reliability of the PDN is introduced. Then, an optimized plan based on proposed method for allocating BESS in IEEE-34 test system is presented. Finally, the simulation results verify the effectiveness and practicability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Sustainable Energy-Tailored Transaction Mechanism for Smart Grids Based on Block Chains
abstract: Developing and implementing sustainable energy is a method to solve energy challenges and eliminate the environmental issues associated with them. It will become the leading source of energy within decades, replacing conventional fossil energy, as many forms of sustainable energy generation coincide nicely with the concept of smart grids. Thus, research of a feasible transaction mechanism for sustainable power generation is necessary. Combining block chain technology and sustainable energy in a smart grid can be a feasible way to manage and utilize sustainable power. In this article, the characteristics and infrastructure of the block chain and state-of-the-art smart grid framework are analyzed, with a sustainable distributed energy transaction mechanism based on block chains presented, designed to achieve the functions of trading, management, and security.

articleTitle: Research on the influence of large scale offshore wind turbines integrated into Jiangsu power system
abstract: In recent years, the great progress has been made in the development of offshore wind power in Jiangsu. The scale of offshore wind power in operation has ranked the first in China, and it is expected that the scale will reach 12870MW in the end of the "14th Five-Year Plan". With the explosion and significant growth of offshore wind power, greater challenges in terms of wind power absorption and system safety will be induced in Jiangsu power system. Simultaneously, the offshore distances of wind power exploitation are getting farther and farther. For some of the approved offshore wind power projects, they will utilize the flexible direct-current (DC) transmission technology to satisfy the demands of long geographical distances. With the widespread application of flexible DC transmission technology in planned offshore wind power projects, the controllability of wind power transmission systems can be improved, but there are also new risks are introduced, such as providing short-circuit currents to the transmission system, sub/super-synchronous oscillations induced from control systems of power electronic equipment and integrated power systems. Considering the development scale of offshore wind power, operation modes and structure characteristics in Jiangsu during "14th Five-Year Plan", influences of large-scale offshore wind turbines integrated to the transmission power system are discussed, through short-circuit currents induced, voltage stability, sub/super-synchronous oscillations. Corresponding improvement measures are put forward.

articleTitle: CONCENTRATED SOLAR POWER COMPARISON FOR POWER TOWER AND PARABOLIC TROUGH SYSTEMS
abstract: South Africa is currently struggling to sustain the power requirements at the consumers' load points. The coal-fired plants are producing emissions at an alarming rate, this has contributed to global warming and acid rain. It is therefore important that more renewable energy-based generating units should be integrated into South Africa's grid system. With the increase of solar power plants connected to the national grid, it is imperative to assess their different topologies as well as their impacts on the distribution power system. South Africa is currently experiencing water shortages and required considerable attention when implementing these systems. Therefore, concentrated solar power (CSP) plant with a storage system connected to the supply network is identified as a feasible solution to improve the performance of the power system. The storage and generation ability as well as the possibility of solar thermal reactors make these systems an ideal choice. The improvement and upgrading of the existing plants can be used to minimize load shedding by stabilizing the grid, creating more jobs and reducing carbon emissions.

articleTitle: Research on Unbalanced Voltage Support of Flexible Current Control Based Three-Phase Four-Wire Converter in Low Voltage Station Area
abstract: Asymmetrical grid fault has negative effects on three-phase four-wire converter connected to low voltage station area such as power oscillation and unbalanced voltage. This paper is more concerned about the unbalanced voltage support at the point of common coupling (PCC). First, through the flexibility of reference current, seven control objectives are achieved by adjusting the control parameters. Then, this paper analyses the principle of PCC voltage support. At the same time, the influences of control strategies on the voltage unbalance factor (VUF) and power oscillation are discussed based on flexible reference current. The seven control objectives have different effects on eliminating active/reactive power oscillation and VUF. It can be found that AP-RPOC has the best output power quality, while NSCC has the best VUF. The simulation results verify the correctness of theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: MoO3@MoS2 Nanosphere as High-Performance Anode Materials for Lithium-lon Batteries
abstract: As a promising electrode material for lithium ion energy storage, metal sulfide oxides with a core-shell nanostructure have high attractiveness. Here, we successfully synthesized MoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> @ MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> core-shell structure material through a simple one-step hydrothermal method. The materials were characterized by scanning electron microscopy, high-resolution transmission electron microscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. MoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> @ MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> used as the negative electrode material of lithium-ion batteries has achieved initial discharge/charge capacities of 1402.5 mA h g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and 1052.4 mA h g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> at a current rate of 0.5C, and the initial coulombic efficiency is about 75.04%. The material exhibits excellent rate performance. When the current rates are 0.2C, 0.5C, 1C, 2C, 5C, and 10C, the specific discharge capacity is 981.1 mA h g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, 866.7 mA h g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, 803.2 mA h g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, 717.0 mA h g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, 603.8 mA h g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and 454.0 mA h g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-l</sup>. This excellent electrochemical performance is mainly attributed to the small-sized nanostructure, which can increase the lithium contact area and the cycle capacity of the battery and the possible interface charging mechanism of the material interface called the pseudocapacitance effect, which not only reduces the repeated cycle process in the mechanical stress, but also provides good electrical conductivity. At the same time, the article also explored the electrochemical performance of MoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> @ MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> as an electrode material for a lithium-ion battery integrated with a negative electrode separator.

articleTitle: TECNORED'S IRRIGATION POWER SUPPLY SYSTEM TECHNOLOGICAL SOLUTION FOR SMALL FARMERS IN CHILE
abstract: This article presents the project carried out by Tecnored's specialized team in order to design and commercialize an energy supply system for irrigation by using photovoltaic energy. This system aims to small farmers in Chile seek the water resource, particularly those in isolated areas which suffer from the problem of the prolonged "mega-drought" that has affected the country since 2010, furthermore the irrigation methods used are not very accessible. In this context, this article accounts for the technological solutions to the irrigation system powered by photovoltaic system that Tecnored has designed to supply energy for small farmers who are out of connection to the grid, contrasting their advantages, disadvantages, and installation costs, with focus on supplying electricity for a daytime irrigation system for 10 years. The study shows that, due to its modularity, ease of maintenance, long service life and low cost, as well as Chile's unique solar conditions, and the government incentives, photovoltaic technology with variable frequency inverters is the most suitable choice for small farmer far from the grid. In addition, the solution is consistent with Chile's commitment to Climate Change and is the most commercially attractive one, which can add product value to clean agricultural production.

articleTitle: Optimal Control Design of VSC-HVDC Systems Integrated with Offshore Wind Farm via Enhanced Equilibrium Optimizer
abstract: A novel enhanced equilibrium optimizer (EEO) for voltage source converter based high voltage direct current (VSC-HVDC) systems integrated with offshore wind farm is developed in this paper. As wind power has inherent characteristic of high uncertainties, its optimal control design becomes a very thorny but also critical task. Conventional PI control framework is widely used which somehow involves many coupled PI gains, while an improper tuning of their values might generally result in a degraded control performance or even a stability collapse in some particular cases. As a result, this work attempts to optimally tune these PI gains through EEO, in which diverse equilibrium candidates are assigned by varying selection probabilities based on their own fitness function rather than a stochastic selection adopted by original equilibrium optimizer (EO), such that a deeper and more effective local exploitation can be realized. Lastly, a case study under power tracking is carried out. Simulation results validate the effectiveness and reliability of EEO compared against that of genetic algorithm (GA).

articleTitle: WIDEBAND IMPEDANCE MODELING AND ANALYSIS OF MODULAR MULTILEVEL CONVERTER CONSIDERING NEGATIVESEQUENCE CONTROL
abstract: Wideband oscillations frequently happened in practical modular multilevel converter based high-voltage dc (MMC-HVDC) transmission systems in recent years. The impedance-based analysis method is an effective tool for revealing the wideband oscillation mechanisms and designing the stabilizing controllers of MMC-HVDC systems. To do that, the wideband impedance model of MMC is prerequisite. A practical MMC-HVDC system with negative-sequence control structure is considered in this paper. The wideband impedance of the MMC is derived based on the harmonic state-space (HSS) method, which includes both the positive- and negative-sequence control strategies as well as the MMC internal dynamics. The derived wideband impedance is validated by frequency scanning in simulation. On this basis, the impact of the negative-sequence control on the impedance characteristics of MMC is analysed and the impact of different positive-negative sequence separation algorithms is also discussed.

articleTitle: A NOVEL CONTROL METHOD BASED ON THE INSTANTANEOUS THYRISTOR VOLTAGE TO MITIGATE COMMUTATION FAILURE IN HVDC SYSTEMS
abstract: Commutation failure is a typical fault that occurs in the inverter valves of the HVDC transmission system. Continuous commutation failure will lead to serious results to the power system especially in multi-infeed HVDC power transmission system. In this paper, a novel control method to mitigate commutation failure in HVDC systems due to voltage dips caused by AC system faults is proposed. This detection method is based on instantaneous values of the thyristor voltage and it is realized by Thyristor Triggering and Monitoring (TTM) device and valve base electronics (VBE), which makes the control system react quickly and detect commutation failure with high-precision. After detecting the commutation failure, the firing angle at the inverter station is reduced by a certain angle to extend the commutation margin. The proposed commutation failure mitigation method is tested in various fault simulation using the PSCAD/EMTDC software. A single-infeed HVDC transmission system is created to test the method's effectiveness and a two-infeed HVDC transmission system is developed to study the method's performance in the multi-infeed HVDC transmission system. The test results demonstrate that the proposed method is highly effective in mitigating the continuous commutation failure in both the single-infeed and multiinfeed HVDC transmission system.

articleTitle: Wind Turbine Operation Condition Identification Method Based on Variable Optimization Selection and Machine Learning
abstract: Effective identification of the operation condition of wind turbines is of great significance to the evaluation of wind turbine power generation performance and the fine management of wind farms. Due to the complex and diverse factors affecting wind turbine operation condition, it is very important to select the appropriate variable set to improve the identification accuracy of wind turbine operation condition. Therefore, a wind turbine operation condition identification method based on variable optimization selection and machine learning is proposed; then, taking the optimal variables under normal operation conditions as input and power as output, the normal behavior model of wind turbines based on BP double hidden layer neural network is constructed; finally, the combined method of DBSCAN clustering algorithm and probability confidence interval is used for residual analysis to realize effective identification of different operation conditions of wind turbines. The results show that the proposed method can deeply dig out the key influencing variables of the wind turbine operation condition, realize the effective identification of the healthy, sub-healthy and abnormal operation conditions, and conform to the actual operation conditions of the wind turbine.

articleTitle: Dynamic Hydraulic Simulation Method of Natural Gas Pipeline Based on the Circuit-Analog Model
abstract: In the research of integrated energy system (IES) security, the problem of dynamic energy flow in different forms of energy network is often encountered. It is a common research idea to transform the problems of non-electric energy network into the problems of power network. In this paper, a finite difference time domain (FDTD) scheme for natural gas transmission equation is proposed based on the solution method of power transmission line equation. Compared with the common Wendroff iterative method, the proposed method has higher efficiency and smaller calculation error, which is verified by a numeral example.

articleTitle: HYBRID WAKE MODEL BASED ON ANALYTICAL MULTI-WAKE MODEL AND CFD MODEL FOR OFFSHORE WIND FARM
abstract: Wake simulation is an extremely critical task in micro-sitting and optimal control of offshore wind farm. The current simulation models principally include analytical multi-wake model and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) model. Analytical multi-wake model has an advantage in its efficiency, and CFD wake model is better in accuracy. Literature show that the CFD model performs well under near wake region. However, the analytical multi-wake model is more suitable in the far wake region. The wind conditions of offshore wind farm are various, single model is not suitable for multi-condition wake simulation. In order to balance simulation accuracy and efficiency, a hybrid model combining the advantages of these two methods has been proposed. Taking Horns Rev offshore wind farm as an example, the results show that hybrid wake model is superior than either of above two models.

articleTitle: Cooperative Control Scheme of Large-scale Distributed PV Grid-connected Systems for Frequency Regulation Based on DC Optimizers
abstract: With the growing proportion of photovoltaic (PV) generation in power systems, DC optimizers (DCOs) based distributed MPPT technologies are recently developed to mitigate the waste of solar energy due to the partial shadow in PV arrays. However, incorporating a large scale of PV capacity into power systems requires frequency regulation enhancement due to the reduced system inertia and PV power fluctuations. In this paper, a novel coordination control strategy for unit-level DCOs and grid-connected inverter is proposed to provide active frequency support from PV units. The proposed control scheme combines the f-P droop control for the power generation of PV-DCO units and the virtual inertia emulation for the DC-link capacitor of the voltage source inverter (VSI), to realize a communication-free cooperative control strategy between large-scale PV systems and grid systems. After that, a flexible power reserve for PV systems is achieved with the improvement of the rate of change of frequency (RoCoF), the frequency nadir, and the steady-state frequency deviation during under/over-frequency events in power systems. Case studies are performed to validate the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Low Voltage Ride-through Strategy for Diode Rectifier Based Hybrid Transmission System
abstract: Compared with the modular multilevel converter (MMC), the number of submodules of the hybrid dc converter based on the diode rectifier (DR) is greatly decreased. Therefore, the economy of offshore dc transmission is significantly increased. During the onshore grid fault, the high-voltage dc (HVDC) link voltage would increase, which cause the submodule capacitors overvoltage. In this paper, a low-voltage-ride-through (LVRT) strategy is proposed for the hybrid DC transmission system. Firstly, the characteristics of offshore ac and dc voltage during the grid fault are analysed. Under the influence of DR, the amplitude of offshore AC voltage would increase with the HVDC link voltage, which makes the offshore wind farms able to perceive the fault status without communication. Then the LVRT strategy is introduced, in which the high-voltage DC chopper of the system is not necessary. The output active power of the offshore wind farm is reduced by the grid-side converter of the wind turbines (WTs) when the fault is detected and the excess power is dissipated by the inner chopper. Finally, the validity of the proposed strategy is verified by the simulation model of the hybrid DC transmission system constructed in the MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Based On-Line Voltage Estimation Method for Distribution Station Area
abstract: Voltage estimation of the station area is the key to timely solve the low-voltage problem in distribution network. Existing voltage estimation methods rely on the collection of grid topology parameters and users' information, and have the disadvantages of complex implementation, poor real-time performance, and large estimation errors. Therefore, a deep learning based on-line voltage estimation method for distribution station area is proposed in this paper. By analyzing the low-voltage formation mechanism in the station area, the main factors affecting the node voltage are summarized. Thereby the key input feature of the feedforward neural network is obtained, which is only the users' active power. Then, the mapping relationship between input feature and node voltage is established based on the self-learning ability of deep learning, and the online voltage estimation of all nodes in the distribution station area can be realized. Finally, the data of typical station are collected to verify the proposed estimation model. The results show that the proposed method can achieve 100% accuracy within the error range of 0.5V. Compared with the traditional voltage estimation methods, the proposed method is more real-time, more efficient and faster without the need of information such as station topology, line parameters, and users' voltage collection.

Index Terms: Activation Function Of The Hidden Layer

articleTitle: MULTI-SCALE PERIODICITY RECOGNITION METHOD OF WIND SPEED BASED ON MORLET WAVELET WITH TIME-FREQUENCY FACTORS
abstract: The volatility of wind speed poses great challenges to the planning and operation of the power system with new energy as the main component. The periodicity of wind speed is an important rule to characterize its fluctuation. However, there are few studies on the periodicity of wind speed, and have no quantitative index to evaluate it at present. To solve the above problems, two quantitative evaluation indexes, periodic intensity (PI) and relative periodic intensity (RPI), are proposed in this paper based on the Morlet wavelet. Furthermore, a time-frequency factor is added in the mother wavelet in order to adapt the periodicity analysis of wind speed which with high variability. The wind speed data of south Gobi, Mongolia is taken as examples to analyse the periodicity of wind speed at multiple time scales, including year, season and month. Then, the wind speed prediction accuracy in different time windows, traditional year time window and the calculated periodic time window, are compared to verify the validity and superiority of the proposed periodicity evaluation indexes. The results show that, the prediction accuracy is improved by 20.51% and 15.79% at two wind measurement points by using the periodic time window.

articleTitle: Multi-Body Dynamic Modeling of Offshore Wind Turbine under Wake Effects
abstract: Due to the challenge of offshore wind farm maintenance and considering economic benefits, the distances between wind turbines in an offshore wind farm cannot be too far. The regular arrangement of turbines will lead to the wake effects and then complex external loads on the turbine including aerodynamic loads and wave loads. Due to the flexible design of large-scale offshore wind turbine blades and the high wind speeds condition, the aerodynamic influences to wind turbines are more significant. A multi-body dynamics models of offshore wind turbines considering wake effects is established in this paper. Improved 2D k Jensen model is used to describe wake profile. Aerodynamic force on the blade is calculated based on BEM theory. Hydrodyn is used to calculate the hydrodynamic force and applied to the downstream turbine model to obtain its dynamic response. The operation performances and loads of the wind turbines under wake effects are obtained. The dynamic model is verified through a comparison between simulation results and the real data from an actual wind farm. Wake effects to aerodynamics of offshore wind turbines are summarized in this paper. This is important to understand the dynamic response and safe operation of offshore wind turbines under wake effect.

articleTitle: SOURCE-GRID COLLABORATED OPTIMAL DISPATCHING APPROACH BASED ON VIRTUAL POWER PLANT
abstract: The high proportion of distributed energy connected to the grid brings challenges to the security and economic operation of the grid. Based on the characteristics of the power supply and cost of distributed generator and distributed energy storage system, aggregated evaluation model of the output range and price of virtual power plants are proposed. And the collaborative optimization method of distribution network with virtual power plant is proposed to promote the participation of distributed energy in the voltage regulation auxiliary service of distribution power network. Taking 24h as the scheduling cycle, considering minimum system voltage deviation, minimum network loss and minimum auxiliary service cost paid to the virtual power plant, the optimization is transformed into a single objective optimization by penalty functions. A time decoupling strategy is proposed to deal with the strong time coupling problem, and the source network collaborative optimization considering the charge-discharge balance of the energy storage device and the limited switching times of the distribution network control equipment is realized. Using improved particle swarm algorithm to solve the optimization model and taking a distributed energy highly penetrated area as an example, the effectiveness of the model and algorithm is verified.

articleTitle: Condition Monitoring of DC-Link Capacitor of Wind Power Converters Based on Pre-charging Circuit
abstract: In view of the difficulty and low accuracy in monitoring the condition of DC-Link capacitors of wind power converters, this paper proposes a quasi-online condition monitoring method based on pre-charging circuit. While the wind power converter starting up, grid-side three-phase currents and DC-side voltage are sampled during the pre-charging process. Then, restructure DC-side current according to the topology of three-phase uncontrolled rectifier, and obtain the corresponding variables related with capacitance of DC-Link capacitor. Finally, the corresponding variables data are adopted for training and testing the model of support vector regression (SVR) to realize the accurate prediction of capacitance, furthermore, to complete condition monitoring of DC-Link capacitor. The proposed method can be implemented by existing sensors and historical data of wind power converter, without extra hardware circuit or changing the control algorithm of converters. The validity is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: POWER GRID PLANNING FRAMEWORK AND APPLICATION PROSPECTS BASED ON DIGITAL TWIN
abstract: With the development of the fourth industrial revolution, digital technologies centered on cloud computing, big data, Internet of Things, mobile Internet, and artificial intelligence are moving towards people's vision. In the era of digital economy, the development of power grids has accelerated and the elements of the system have changed more, and the traditional grid planning methods are no longer applicable to the development environment of power grids at this stage. In this paper, digital twins are introduced into power grid planning, and a framework and process of power grid planning based on digital twins are constructed to change the inherent methodology of power grid planning from the perspective of top-level design. The aim of this paper is to give a solution to the new trend of grid planning through the construction of a framework. The digital twins enables the grid to adapt to rapid changes in the environment through real-time interaction between the digital and physical worlds. Relevant digital twins platforms are also presented, including Azure, Maple, Simulink, etc. The paper also provides an outlook on the application of digital twins in grid planning, describing the advantages, difficulties and development trends of the application.

articleTitle: Mitigation of SSCI in the DFIG Based Large Scale Wind Power System with Optimized Multimode Damping Controller
abstract: In this paper, a grid-side suppression strategy is proposed for Guyuan wind farm, by adding the Sub-synchronous control interaction(SSCI) damping controller to the STATCOM of the wind farm. Firstly, the basic modelling and general characteristic of SSCI in a typical wind power system is firstly introduced. And the control-design task is formulated into a complex nonlinear optimization problem with many operation conditions. Then, a combination of genetic algorithm and simulated annealing, namely GA-SA, is proposed to solve the nonlinear optimization problem for multi-operation state. The performance of the proposed scheme is validated on an aggregated model of the actual wind power system using Simulink environment. The time-domain simulations have demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed scheme for mitigating the SSCI at various oscillation frequencies.
